The sixth arrangement — this is the day on which all this palanquin was set in order; and it has no ordering and no strength except from this day. When this [day] came, it ordered this palanquin with many spirits, with many souls, with many beautiful maidens, fair in appearance, those fitting to dwell in the palace of the King. It too was set in order in beauty [more than] all the other days that were before, and it ordered them in a single desire, in [good] will, in joy — the ordering of above and below. Then this palanquin was sanctified with supernal sanctifications and adorned with its crowns, until it ascended in the ascent of the crown of rest, and is called by the supernal Name, the holy Name, which is Sabbath — the rest of all, the desire of all, the cleaving of all, of above and below as one. And then it is written, 'King Solomon made himself a palanquin of the cedars of Lebanon.'" Thus far [the Zohar's] words.

And although the passage requires a long explanation, as will be explained in the book Or Yakar, with God's help, even so from within it it is implied explicitly that all the utterances and the creations were by [means of] the six days. "Let there be light, and there was light" is in Chesed, etc. — it is found that, even if we say that "In the beginning" is an utterance, no matter at all remains for the three first [Sefirot]. And therefore it is necessary to clear away the stumbling-stones of the difficulties from these utterances, and to set this exposition upon its proper proportion. And first of all let us say that one cannot deny that the creations of the account of Creation were in six days, as in "and there was evening and there was morning, one day," "a second day," etc. — indicating that, although there were ten utterances, all the same they were included within the six days. Now, let us know: if it is true that "In the beginning" is an utterance — be it in Chokhmah or in Keter — how can it be right [that] there, it said, "and the earth was unformed and void, and darkness," etc.? Would it seem good in the eyes of YHVH that we should say that, when Malkhut was in Chokhmah or in Keter, the husks [kelipot] surrounded it there — namely, unformed-ness and void and darkness? This is surely a great strain, for who placed a husk above? And now, surely the matter is this: that the Torah informed us, first of all, of the existence of the Emanation, in the order of its emanation in general. And this is the meaning of the verse "In the beginning" (Bereshit), whose meaning is: the concealed Keter, together with the "beginning" (reshit), which is Chokhmah, created and emanated — "[and] God" (Elohim), which is Binah — "the heavens," which are Chesed and Tiferet. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the word "et" comes to include Chesed; and "the heavens" [is] Tiferet. "And et the earth" — that is, Gevurah, by the inclusion of "et"; and "the earth" is Malkhut. And Netzach and Hod and Yesod are included in Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And afterward it said, "and the earth was unformed and void," etc., which is to inform us of the existence of Malkhut and its chariots, good and evil. And afterward it informed us of the actions of these Sefirot in Malkhut. And because the three first [Sefirot] are concealed and have no revealed action, their action and their utterance was drawn forth by means of the three Patriarchs, who are the three craftsmen — Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet. And therefore "Let there be light" is the first utterance, and it is drawn from Keter by means of Gedulah to the palanquin. [And the second utterance, "Let there be a firmament," is drawn from Chokhmah by means of Gevurah to the palanquin; and therefore, etc. — see in Asis Rimmonim and in [the commentary] Pelach.] And therefore the matter of the firmament that separates between water and water is found to be alluded to, at times, in Chokhmah, in the secret of the upper waters and the lower waters, with the firmament in between, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, with God's help. And the third utterance, "Let the waters be gathered," is from Binah by means of Tiferet; and this is the substance of the passage of the Tikkunim. Now let us say that the fourth utterance, which is on the third day, and which is the utterance "Let the earth sprout," is drawn from Chesed by means of Tiferet — the third day. And the utterance "Let there be luminaries" is drawn from Gevurah — as is known, [the word] "luminaries" (me'orot) is [written] defective, on account of Gevurah — and was made by means of Netzach, the fourth day. And the utterance "Let the waters swarm" is drawn from Tiferet by means of Netzach within Hod. And this is alluded to in the passage of Terumah that we copied above, where it said, "the fourth arrangement was drawn — the light of the sun," that is, the existence of Tiferet. And the reason is that, because Tiferet is composed of right and left, it received three utterances from Chesed and Gevurah, and one of its own; and for the reason that it inclines toward Chesed, it performed one utterance in Chesed — and that is the utterance "Let the earth sprout," which is the second on the third day and the fourth among the utterances, which is in Chesed; and it delivered to Netzach two utterances, which are the fifth, of Gevurah, and the sixth, of itself. Netzach performed the fifth, of Gevurah, and delivered to Hod the sixth, of Tiferet. And because there is no completeness of judgment except with mercy, therefore the light of the sun did not shine by means of Netzach, and the action of Netzach was not complete, until the fifth day came — which is Hod — in which the sixth utterance was made, which is the utterance of Tiferet. And this is what it said in the passage of Terumah: "in the fifth arrangement, and it performed service to bring forth that light in the arrangement of the fourth day," etc. And Yesod, which is the sixth day — because it includes Netzach and Hod — brought forth three utterances, which correspond to Netzach-Hod-Yesod: namely, the utterance "Let the earth bring forth" corresponding to Netzach, the utterance "Let us make man" corresponding to Hod, and the utterance "Behold, I have given" corresponding to Yesod. For the utterance "Be fruitful and multiply" is not an utterance, but is only a blessing — for if not [so], there would be literally ten utterances [of creation], and how could it say "there are nine"? Rather, surely, according to this view, it is not called an utterance, but [only] an utterance of creation [proper]; and this [other] is an utterance of blessing. And because the matter of fruitfulness and multiplication is in Yesod, therefore this blessing was placed on the sixth [day], which is Yesod. And by this the Sabbath day, which is Malkhut, was sanctified, and was included and built — "a city [rebuilt] upon its mound." And after she was completed, she said her [own] utterance, which is, "It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make for him," etc. — for by means of the coupling the blessing would be made to flow, as is proved in the Zohar in many places. And now it is found that, as for the allusion of the utterances themselves — which are the agents in the ten Sefirot — the utterances are only nine; for the utterance "It is not good" is not [the utterance of] Malkhut itself, but [is] the actions of Malkhut; and the utterance of Malkhut is the one that was decreed from the mouth of Yesod, for Yesod emanated Malkhut. And because, in the passage of the Talmud in Rosh Hashanah that we dealt with, the intent was that the ten Kingships are literally ten utterances — therefore [the questioner] objected and said, "these are [only] nine" — for the utterance "Let there be light" is Chokhmah, as is explained in the Zohar in many places, and it issues from the power of Keter; and his intent is not literally Chokhmah, but the utterances drawn forth to Malkhut: what was drawn from Keter was the existence of Chokhmah, and what was drawn from Chokhmah was the existence of Binah. And therefore he objected, "these are [only] nine," for the utterance drawn from Malkhut — which is "It is not good for the man to be alone" — is not [that of] Malkhut, but [is] what is drawn from Malkhut. Therefore the allusion of the utterances in the Sefirot themselves is only nine. And to this he answered, "In the beginning is also an utterance" — for although it is the existence of the Emanation, the matter was [bound up] with Keter, and it is impossible that Keter not be included there, as we explained. And now it can rightly be [understood] what is found in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit, and in the Tikkunim: that this utterance at times alludes to Keter, at times to Chokhmah, at times to Binah, at times to Malkhut — which is also called "beginning" (reshit) — at times to Da'at; [this] being an utterance that comprehends the existence of the whole Emanation in its entirety, as we explained. And by this we have fulfilled our obligation, at a time such as this, regarding this matter, so that the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, not be in dispute, some of them with others, and so that there be no dispute, God forbid, with what was explained in the Gemara in these passages — so as not to give an opening to those who speak falsehood. And let each man come to his place in peace and rest upon his bed.

Now, after we have cleared the stumbling-stones from the vineyard of this passage in the preceding chapters, let us examine it somewhat, and afterward explain its intent in brief, with the help of God. And what there is to examine is [as follows]. First: regarding the order of the sages — that [the Talmud] placed Rav Yosef before Rabbi Yochanan, whereas Rabbi Yochanan preceded him by a long time. Second: since the Commandments and the utterances and the praises all allude to the ten Sefirot, then in what do they [the three sages] differ? Third: their saying "ten praises that David said in the book of Psalms" — which is prolixity without benefit, for it is surely [the case] that David said praises only in the book of Psalms — to the point that, almost, by this prolixity, room was given to err, [namely] that [the questioner] objected to him, "there are many praises," since the questioner understood, from what was said "in the book of Psalms," that the intent was the whole book. Fourth: their saying "the Ten Commandments that were spoken to Moses at Sinai" — why did he prolong [it] so? Are there others? And what there is further to examine in his language will be explained according to our way, with God's help. And this passage will be understood together with what has preceded us in the Tikkunim, where Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the Kingships are in Malkhut, the Remembrances in Tiferet, and the Shofarot in Binah. And even if there are other explanations of this among the later commentators, even so they all agreed that the Kingships are in Malkhut; and the questioner already had it as preceding [knowledge] that surely the ten Kingships are in the ten Sefirot. But he was in doubt whether they would be the ten Sefirot included within Malkhut itself — in the manner that each one is composed of ten, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, ch.2, with God's help — or whether they would be the ten Sefirot themselves, but their existence [would be] in their effluence into Malkhut; or [whether] we should say that the Sefirot are literally in their [own] place. And if you say that they are called "Kingships," and [that] it is necessary that they be in Malkhut, for their name proves [it] concerning them — we answer that they would be ten Kingships, which are the Malkhut [aspect] in each and every Sefirah, in its [own] place. And according to these ways we shall explain regarding the Remembrances and the Shofarot, as explained. And this is what is [meant by] "These ten Kingships — corresponding to what?": since they are ten, I know that their number proves concerning them that they are [set] against the ten Sefirot; but the question is, in which aspect of them, among these three aspects that we mentioned. And in this the three sages differed — this one says [it is] in this [aspect], and this one says [it is] in this [aspect]. And Rebbi answered that they are against the ten praises that David said in the book of Psalms. And he intended, by the prolixity of his language, "that David said," [to point] to what our Sages of blessed memory already explained: that all that David said in the book of Psalms, he said only against Malkhut, which was his attribute.

Now he intended the first aspect, which is the ten Sefirot included within Malkhut, as we explained. And the questioner did not understand the precision of the [poetic] phrasing in his saying "in the book of Psalms," and likened it to an intent of indicating a [specific] place; and therefore he objected, "there are many." And [the Talmud] answered him that he intended only those in which a shofar is mentioned — and they are at the end of the book: "Praise El in His sanctuary" is Keter; "praise Him in the firmament of His might" is Chokhmah; "praise Him in His mighty acts" is Binah; "praise Him according to His abundant greatness" is Gedulah; "praise Him with the blast of the shofar" is Gevurah; "praise Him with harp and lyre" is Tiferet; "praise Him with drum and dance" is Netzach; "praise Him with strings and pipe" is Hod; "praise Him with sounding cymbals" is Yesod; "praise Him with cymbals of acclamation" is Malkhut. And all these are in Malkhut, as is proved from their being in the book of Psalms, which is against Malkhut. And Rav Yosef intended the second aspect — which is that the intent, in [the] ten Kingships, is that the Sefirot all emanate into Malkhut; and this he intended in saying "against the Ten Commandments," etc. And it has been explained that, at the giving of the Torah, each attribute of the attributes emanated one Commandment of the Commandments into the Sefirah [of] Malkhut, and Malkhut revealed that Commandment and showed it to Israel. And this is [the meaning of] what is said (Exodus 20:15), "and all the people saw the sounds (voices)": they saw the sounds coming to Malkhut, so that Malkhut would speak the Commandment by the power of each and every Sefirah. And this Rashbi, peace be upon him, intended in the book of the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 10), and these are his words: "And on the seventh day the Torah was given — this is the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world; and in his grade, Malkhut, [he] spoke with them. And they have already established it: ten kings — lest they not be able to speak with one mouth — 'He touched [the letter] alef in [the word] bayit,' and [thus] included in her all the ten."

Now the intent is explained, without our examining his language now, so as not to be lengthy. And further, because [Malkhut] spoke from the side of Malkhut, for she was the one who spoke, [acting] from the power of each and every Sefirah that emanates into her. And this Rav Yosef intended in saying "the Ten Commandments that were spoken to Moses at Sinai" — and the intent is that they were spoken to him by means of Sinai, which is Malkhut, as explained. And it is no wonder how they are ten apart from Malkhut, for Malkhut has an aspect [together] with the ten, and an aspect receiving from the ten, in that she receives from herself, in the secret of the existence of the yod and the heh that are within her, as will be explained in the Gate of Existence. And by this the language of Rashbi, peace be upon him, will be made precise, in his saying "He touched [the letter] in [the word] bayit" — for the existence of the bet in Malkhut is the existence of the heh, and they are lower grades within her, in respect of the aspect of the yod, as will be explained in the aforementioned Gate. And therefore he said "and included in her all the ten," for even Malkhut needs to be included with her.

Now Rav Yosef intended the second aspect, which is the ten Sefirot emanating into Malkhut. And Rabbi Yochanan intended the third aspect, which is the aspect of the Sefirot themselves in their [own] place. And this he intended in saying "By ten utterances the world was created" — which are the essences of the Sefirot in their [own] place. And what is intended by Malkhut is that, when we are at the Kingships, we direct [our intent] toward the ten Sefirot in their [own] place, or toward the Malkhut [aspect] in each and every Sefirah, as we explained above.

And the matter of "there are nine" has been explained above. And he answered, "In the beginning is also an utterance" — for although it speaks of the existence of the Emanation, even so it is the existence of an utterance; and the necessity for this is in "[By] the word of YHVH the heavens were made": the explanation being that the existence of the Emanation [of] "the heavens," which are Tiferet, [is that] their emanation is from Keter, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with the help of God.
Now [Scripture] used, regarding this, the expression "by the word" — a term of utterance — [to teach] that the existence of the Emanation is related [to the category of] utterance.

Thus, from this passage it appears explicitly that the existence of the ten Commandments, and the ten utterances, and the ten praises are faithful witnesses, in our holy Torah, to the existence of the ten Sefirot, without any doubt whatsoever — apart from what we wrote in the preceding Gate, in chapter 1, with God's help. And no question remains in this regard for our received tradition, to say that perhaps they are twenty or five, at all.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, established that there is no room to ask for a necessity-[proof] for our received tradition — for we have an absolute necessity, as explained — let us say that likewise there is no [room] to ask the Emanator a reason: why did He emanate ten, and not twenty, and not five, and the like. (Nor does the question arise, since "the very root of the law is [open to] refutation.") And it is fitting that we inquire into this whole Emanation: why was it emanated? And with our answer in this, all will be settled. And it is this: that the intent of the Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, [was] to bring within limit the things that are not within limit — that is, the Emanator is without end, and the intent of the Emanator in the creation of this lowly world [was] that the world be possessed of an end, perishing and passing away. And for this reason the Emanation was necessitated: so that, by means of the emanated [beings] being emanated and the grades being chained down, grade after grade — emanated from emanator, created from emanated, formed from created, made from formed — until the grades reach the corruption and the perishing that they are in. For there is a created being that came into being in a night and perished in a night; and there is [one] that, though it stand a day or two days, will not endure. And now, how can clay say to its fashioner, "why thus and not thus?" — and He saw, in His wisdom, that it is impossible to reach the [final] end of the comings-into-being and perishings of the creatures unless the number of the emanated [beings] be ten. For if they were fewer than ten, the creatures would not descend to that grade of descent, on account of their nearness to the source. And now, since all that is possible in the Emanation has been emanated, it is necessitated that the grades chained down from them descend to the [final] end — because they grow distant from the root as much as is needed to come to an end. And it is not our intent to say that the emanated [beings] are possessors of limit and end, God forbid; rather, our intent is that the actions that proceed from them perform a finite action, like the action of this world, which comes into being and perishes and is possessed of limit and measure — acted [upon] by the agents by means of the creatures [derived] from the emanated. And the need for the end and the limit in the lower comings-into-being, our Sages of blessed memory explained in the Mishnah, in their saying, "By ten utterances the world was created — and what does the text teach [by this]? Could it not have been created by a single utterance?" That is, it was not impossible, God forbid, for the creation of this world to be by a single utterance that would comprehend all the things and grades and creations and comings-into-being that have now come to be. For although some of the actions are by means of Chesed and some by means of Gevurah, and so from all of them, the power of creation by means of a single utterance would not, on this account, be lacking — for the power of all of them is in each one of them, as is known, each being composed of ten, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, ch.2, with God's help. And the reason it required ten utterances is "in order to exact [punishment]" — that is, that by means of the ten utterances the creatures descended to an end; for if they were not possessed of an end, then a person would live forever and would not receive punishment for his iniquities, and the side of impurity and the husk would spread in the world, and the corruption would not be rectified. And likewise the righteous would be sunk in this world and would not see good. Therefore it was required that the world be possessed of an end and limit, in order to exact [punishment] from the wicked and to give good reward to the righteous. And the explanation of "that they destroy the world that was created," etc. — the meaning is that they destroy the world and have the power to consume it, because it is possessed of an end and was created by ten utterances. And likewise the righteous uphold it — for if it were not possessed of an end, the righteous would not uphold it nor the wicked destroy it. For this it was necessitated that it be created by ten utterances — namely, the emanation of ten grades, in order that it be possessed of an end; and the wicked one perishes and is lost and returns to his dust and is rectified, and the righteous one departs in honor, to greet the face of his Father in Heaven and to eat the fruit of his deeds. However, there is a difficulty with this reason: that if so — [if] the cause of the Emanation was to bring the lower comings-into-being to corruption and perishing, in order to reward the doers of righteousness at all times and to punish the wicked, as explained — then after the resurrection, which is not a time of reward and punishment and is not a time of [the performance of] deeds, as is known, what reason is there for the Emanation? For wickedness has already ceased from the earth, and it is the time of endurance. Shall we say that the intent of the Emanation was only until the time of the resurrection? God forbid — this is surely not [so], for the essence of the world and its perfection is then, as is known; and then, surely, will be the perfection of the Emanation and its illumination. And like this difficulty, [there is] also a difficulty regarding the holy palaces, in which a person is judged according to his deeds, to reward him and to punish him, as will be explained in the Gate of the Holy Palaces, with God's help — and if so, in the time of the resurrection, when there is no rewarding and punishing and judging and contending over the children of men, what will be the matter of the palaces? Shall we say that they will be in vain, and each one will cease from his work that they perform? And even so, this is no question — for it is possible that they be unified, each with its fellow, this within that and that within this, "each man cleaving to his brother," and in the time of their oneness and union there is no judgment in them, and the sparks are absorbed into their sources, and they delight in great peace, as is explained in Parashat Pekudei concerning the matter of the palaces, in the Zohar. And for this reason too, one cannot say that the intent of the Emanation was to reward and to punish, to judge and to contend over the liable and the meritorious — for if so, we would ask: since after the resurrection there is no judging of the children of men according to their deeds, but rather they delight in what they toiled [for] on the eve of the Sabbath [i.e., in this world], then it is found, God forbid, that their matter would be in vain. Therefore let us say that the essence of their emanation was not for this matter — even though reward and punishment proceed from them, by the supernal providence, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance and in the Gate of Essence and Vessels. Rather, the essence of the intent was to make His divinity known to that which is other than Himself, as we shall explain in the second reason in this chapter, and we shall add explanation in ch.7, with God's help. And by this it is found that, on the contrary, all the while that the world is in corruption from the filth of the serpent and the husk, the emanated [beings] are not unified as is fitting, and His divinity is not revealed, and the knowledge among the people of the children of Israel is utterly consumed — until [He] have mercy from Heaven, and the world go forth from the filth of the serpent and be rectified as is fitting; and then the world will return to its rectification, and His divinity will be revealed among the lower [beings] properly and rightly, and the children of men will increase in strength in the knowledge of Him. And then it will be said (Jeremiah 31), "and they shall teach no more, each man his fellow," etc., "for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them." And then the light of the Torah and its hidden things and its secrets will be revealed properly and rightly, and the emanated [beings] will be united in perfect union — for the verse will be fulfilled that is written (Zechariah 14), "and YHVH shall be King over all the earth; on that day YHVH shall be one and His name one." And from the Mishnah of the ten utterances nothing can be inferred [to the contrary], for it is possible that this is its meaning: "By ten utterances the world was created" — that is, all the ten Sefirot acted in the creation of the world, although it was possible, by the power of one [of them], to be created — namely Keter, which is called "one utterance," as explained in the Zohar. "But [it was] in order [to exact punishment]," etc. — that is, because they could perform actions in differing aspects, whether for judgment or for mercy; and Keter has no judgment in it, but [only] simple mercy, as is known. And the intent in this Mishnah is not that the emanation of the emanated [beings] was for the sake of the world, God forbid, but it is a reason for their action below, in the lower world, although there is power in the first Sefirah to perform everything. Furthermore, [there is] another reason, close to the preceding: that the Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He — His attribute is to emanate effluence to that which is other than Himself, and that His good effluence [is] to do good to the creatures and to emanate to them of His attributes, like Chesed by the attribute of Chesed, and so for all the Sefirot. And He saw [fit] to emanate this Emanation and to reveal His greatness to the eyes of the creatures, so that He would be recognized by His creatures and somewhat apprehended by means of His holy and pure Emanation; and this is of His good attributes — His will being to reveal His exaltedness to the lowly [beings]. And because, in the revealing of His exaltedness in Keter to the creatures, on account of the great exaltedness of the emanated [Keter], there is still no power in the creatures to apprehend Him, it was necessary to emanate Chokhmah; and likewise from Chokhmah to Binah, until Malkhut — for there [is] the apprehension of the exaltedness of the King. And the parable for this: [it is] like a ray of the sun entering through an aperture into the house to illumine the inner side of the house; and on account of its great brightness, no one in the house can bear it, and their eyes are dimmed from looking at the sun, for it is great and dazzles exceedingly — until they are required to make there a very large lantern, so that the light would illumine toward its inner side, and the benefit of the light, and not the harm, would reach those standing in the house. And on account of the great brightness of the light of the sun in its strength and might — although the light has been somewhat sweetened and hidden and somewhat concealed — even so, for the weakness of the sight of those standing in the house, they need a second screen, and from the second a third, up to ten. And now, when a man comes into the house to benefit from the light that illumines through the lantern, and asks why the number of these lanterns was such-and-such and not such-and-such, we would blunt his teeth and say to him that out of his great foolishness he asked about this matter. For since the matter of the screens — its intent is to rectify the matter of the light, so that it be sweetened to the eyes of the beholders — then if the screens are reduced, the eye of the beholder is darkened by the abundance of [the light's] brightness, and it is harmed; and if they are increased upon them further, the light is darkened, and the sweetness of its light does not reach the beholders, and the eyes are darkened at the apertures. And the intent is not so, but [rather] to rectify the light so that they may benefit from it as brightly as possible, and that there be nothing in [its] existence that would harm by the abundance of brightness, but [rather] a bright light, a sweet light, a perfumed light. And a compelling proof for this reason is found in a passage from the Zohar that we shall copy in the Gate of Essence and Vessels, with God's help — and it is the passage, "To whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" etc. And there we explained, in the exposition of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the essence of the Emanation is "so that they may know Him," etc. — for by means of the Sefirot His greatness is revealed to us. And not as we have seen the philosophers, masters of darkness and confusion: that, because of the removal of the predicates, the providence of divinity was hidden from their eyes, and they thought that they had apprehended Him while their heart was far from Him — because of their error concerning the truth of the Ein Sof, blessed be He [that, on account of His great greatness and exaltedness, He would not exercise providence over the lower beings] — and by this they deny His providence and most of His matters and actions in this world. And not like these is the portion of Jacob, for He is the fashioner of all. And the matters of His predicates, and His sitting and His rising and His going and His speaking and all that resembles these, are understood to those who know the wisdom, and will be explained at length in the coming Gates, with God's help.

After God has favored us in the preceding chapters, and we have explained, concerning the reason for the Emanation, a thing seemly and acceptable, and established it in the words of our Sages of blessed memory — our wish, in this chapter, is to prolong the matter and broaden it in this, with God's help, in a manner that the eyes of the inquirer be enlightened in this matter. And before we come to the explanation of this matter, let us ask one question, in which some of the inquirers of the wisdom have been perplexed. And it is: whether there is ability in the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, to emanate ten Sefirot other than these, or not, God forbid.

Now it is fitting that we inquire: if He is able — since His attribute of goodness is to emanate effluence to that which is other than Himself — why did He not emanate even a thousand thousands of thousands [of Sefirot], since it is within possibility, within His ability, and He could emanate several times ten Sefirot and several worlds, in the manner that He brought this world into existence? And on its face, this question would alarm the eyes of the enlightened and astonish him. But the truth is that this question is a question of great foolishness, and out of much ignorance the questioner asked this question. And the reason — let us say to the one who asks this question: that his question cannot escape [being one] of three things. Either he asks that the second Sefirot be equal to the true, emanated Sefirot — that is, Keter equal to Keter, Chokhmah equal to Chokhmah, Binah equal to Binah, and so all of them; or that they be greater than them — that is, finer than them; or that they be smaller than them, and revealed. And now, these three aspects cannot be. Because the Sefirot are fine, the utmost of fineness — that is, spiritual, the utmost of spirituality, free of body and of the corporeal and its accidents, as we explained and as we shall explain in the Gate of Gates. And since this matter is true, that they are not bodies, then they cannot be distinguished from the Emanator and [yet] be included in the number of the ten, except by way of cause and effect — that is, the Emanator [is] a cause to the emanated [beings]; thus there is a difference between Him and His emanated [beings]. And apart from other differences, with whose explanation we have no concern now.

Now Keter is distinguished from Chokhmah in that Chokhmah is an effect of Keter, and Keter is a cause to Chokhmah; and so is their distinction, one from another, down to the lowest grade — for apart from this matter they have no distinction by which to be included in the number ten, since that which is not a body is not divided into parts, as we shall expand on this matter in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, with God's help. And now, when the questioner says that the [other] ten Sefirot would be equal to these, we answer him that it is impossible. For since Keter is equal to Keter, there cannot be two Keters — for if so, by what would they be distinguished, so as to be two? If so, there cannot be emanated, from the one unique Emanator, [more] than one emanated [being]. For two is impossible, since there is no distinction between them — for both are effects of the First Cause; for if not [so], they are not spiritual, and if they are spiritual, they cannot be two. If so, it is necessitated that there be emanated from the Emanator [no more than] one emanated [being]. And in this manner we answer regarding Chokhmah with Chokhmah, and so for all the Sefirot — until we necessitate that there cannot be [Sefirot] other than these ten Sefirot. And let not this question arise — that if so, God forbid, there is no power in the Emanator to emanate two Keters [that are] effects of Him, equal, and that would be distinguished one from another while being equal — for this is foolishness. For this matter is not on account of a deficiency and a weakening of ability, God forbid, neither in the Emanator nor in the emanated [beings]; but on the contrary, it is their praise. For in order to be distinguished, they would need to descend to the baseness of body, which is divided into parts — and this is not fitting. For from the greatness of the servant the greatness of the master is known, and it is of his [the master's] perfection to perfect that which is other than himself. And one should not ask: on the contrary, we would [the better] know and recognize His excellence [if], without a body to corporealize Him, and from His being simple and not possessed of body, as is known, He should bring into existence body and corporeality and emanate two Keters, and they be corporeal. For to this we answer you: He has already created much of this kind — namely the angels, which are corporeal in truth, although their corporeality is fine, like the corporeality of fire and finer than it, as was explained in the Gate of Palaces. And one should also not ask that He impress upon the spiritual [the property] that, though it be fine and spiritual, it be divided into parts — for this matter would be the deficiency in the spiritual, since the essence of its perfection is in its oneness and its being indivisible. And the parable for this: that the questioner does not ask whether there is power in the king to be a servant, and [whether], since the ability of the servant is not in him, the servant is [therefore] found more praiseworthy than he. For on the contrary, there is indeed [such power]; but if he did this, it would be a baseness and a deficiency in the crown of kingship; and the honor of the king is to distance himself from all the kinds of the service of servants. And so is the matter with the Emanator and the emanated [beings]: for it is the praise of the Emanator to impress upon the emanated [beings] the power of His seal — that they be simple, not composite, and far from corporeality and from all its accidents.

Now [thus] we have established that for them to be equal is impossible. And now let us say that to ask, likewise, that they be greater than these — his question is not right, nor is there truth in his words. For there is no distinction between the Emanator and the emanated except the distinction that is between cause and effect; and as much as it is possible for the emanated to be near to the Emanator, Keter has been brought near — until there remains no room to say that there should be an emanated [being] between Keter and the Emanator, but [only] that this is a cause and this is an effect; and this is the necessity of its descent from the degree of the Emanator, although it [Keter] is great without end, for it is dark before its Emanator, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And there is no room to ask why the Ein Sof did not emanate Keter [to be] exactly equal to Him, since no power is lacking — because the truth is that it is impossible for the emanated to be equal to the Emanator. And this is not on account of a deficiency of the Emanator, but on account of the nature of the emanated. For since it is emanated, it is an effect of its cause, and its cause is above it, with a certain priority in several matters that it is impossible for an effect to apprehend [in] its cause; and if so, it is necessitated of it that, being emanated and an effect, it descend from before the face of its Master, like the difference between cause and effect; and this caused it its deficiency — that it is emanated and an effect, and a First Cause precedes it. And if so, by this is also negated the question to say that that [hypothetical] Keter should be greater than this Keter, since this Keter is the greatest possible within the [class of] the emanated. And likewise, to say that it should be lesser than this is impossible — for there is already [one] lesser than it, which is Chokhmah; and what rises above Chokhmah is Keter. That is: since Chokhmah is an effect of Keter and does not descend from Keter except [by] what is between cause and effect, it is impossible to ask that there be another emanated [being] between Chokhmah and Keter. For this [hypothetical] emanated [being], [being] equal to Keter, is impossible for it to be, and not equal to Chokhmah, for the reason we explained. Between Keter and Chokhmah is impossible, because Keter and Chokhmah are cause and effect, and there is no distinction between them that could bear an effect prior to Chokhmah and posterior to Keter — unless Chokhmah were to descend to the place of Binah, namely the third effect, and if so this would be Chokhmah and Binah. And by this all the questions are removed, entirely.

And now let us explain that which we roused concerning the matter of the three aspects in each Sefirah — which we shall expand on in the coming Gates, with God's help — and they are these: that for each and every Sefirah there are three aspects: first, its aspect in respect of what is emanated from it; second, in respect of itself; third, in respect of its emanator. And the matter is that, in Keter itself — since it is emanated from the Emanator, who is Emanator and not emanated, prolixity about whom is surely forbidden, and may God forgive what we have prolonged about Him until now — [and] so, in Chokhmah, emanated from Keter, there was necessitated to be in it an aspect of equalization — that is, a nearness uniting with its emanator, which is Keter, where there is no distinction between them at all; and after this it itself descends, and is distinguished from itself to itself, until it comes to be a cause [to] Binah, the effect [emanated] from it.

Now in it [Chokhmah] itself there is necessitated to be in it an aspect [going] from cause to effect, that it ascend from aspect to aspect, ever higher and higher. And the parable for this: the aspect equalized to Keter is the cause to the aspect of its [own] essence, and the aspect of its essence is the cause to [the aspect] that equalizes it to Binah [and likewise, in each and every aspect, there will be these very three aspects, from cause to effect]; and between every two aspects there are necessitated, further, three aspects — namely, the first aspect, equalized to Keter; and the aspect itself; and the aspect equalizing it to its [own] essence. And let us depict a corporeal form, from which the intellect may ascend to the spiritual — as though we depict a "head of a row" (a triangular wedge), which is this elongated triangle.

Now this triangle slopes and descends, and from its upper side it widens — it is a parable for the emanated [beings], [in] that, the more they draw near to their source, the more they are elevated and widened: not a corporeal, bounded width, but a width in fineness and spirituality.

Now when the inquirer looks well, he will find that the uppermost [part] of Keter is wide and slopes and narrows and continues until its width comes to equal the width of Chokhmah. And even at the place of the equalization of Keter and Chokhmah there is a great distinction — for so it was necessitated from the side of the emanator that emanates and descends, [in] that there is no standstill to its descent; for the more it grows distant from the supernal Face, the more the emanated is revealed and is caused [to revolve] from its supernal causer; and this is cause and effect, for one who has eyes of intellect and whom God has favored with knowledge. And this is the secret of "each one composed of ten," and the secret of the descent of the grades within the essence of the Sefirot themselves. For Keter-of-Keter is the side that draws near to the Emanator, and Malkhut-of-Keter is the side that draws near to Chokhmah; and Keter-of-Chokhmah is an effect of Malkhut-of-Keter. And all this is recognized from the form that we depicted. For the narrow [part] of Keter is a cause to the wide [part] of Chokhmah; and likewise Keter-of-Chokhmah is the side that draws near to Keter; and Malkhut-of-Chokhmah is the side that draws near to Binah; and Keter-of-Binah is an effect of Malkhut-of-Chokhmah. And in this likeness too one must say that each and every part is composed of ten Sefirot — also because there is no standstill to the light, but [it] grows distant and descends; and each and every point, and each and every part, is a cause to the point below it and an effect of the point above it. And He saw, in His wisdom, that if Keter itself did not descend ten degrees, it would be impossible for Chokhmah to be emanated from it at all. And likewise, if Chokhmah did not descend ten degrees, it would not be within possibility for Binah to be emanated from it. And so for all the Sefirot, and so for all the parts and the points. And this is the law and this is the reason for ABY"A: for in Atzilut there is ABY"A, and in Beriah there is ABY"A, and in Yetzirah ABY"A, and in Asiyah ABY"A. For the matter of ABY"A is [that they are] the sum of all that is distinguished from the First Necessary [Being], the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He — from Keter to the central point at the navel of the earth; and they are the kinds of their descent in four grades. And likewise each one of them, when we come to divide them, we divide into four grades; and likewise each and every grade into four grades — except that the four of Atzilut are so fine that the Asiyah-of-Atzilut is a cause and a source to the Atzilut-of-Beriah, and likewise the Asiyah-of-Beriah is a cause and a source to the Atzilut-of-Yetzirah, and so in this order [for] all the grades and all the parts — until the [whole] existence is found [to be] like a lamp of segments [a jointed lampstand], uniting and embracing one another, "each man [with] his brother," as explained. And after we have roused [discussion] on this, my wish in this matter [is] to rouse [it] regarding the question of the number of the ten, which we asked in the preceding chapters: it is known that every effect is encompassed by its cause, and the cause encompasses the effect, as we shall expand in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, with God's help. And now let us depict a corporeal form, namely a circle within a circle, like this:

[such] that the space does not pass between these spheres. And now, should the questioner ask why this draftsman did not draw, within these circles, yet other circles — surely we would blunt his teeth and say to him that "he has gathered the wind in his fists" [Proverbs 30:4]: for it is impossible for there to be a further addition to the count of circles, since they descend one from another like a point, and it is impossible, in [their] existence, for there to be yet [another] circle within the great circle that encompasses them all within it.

Now from the corporeal form let us elevate our intellect to the spiritual, which we are in the [course of] explaining. It is known that the Sefirot descend one from another like the distinction between cause and effect; and therefore they are one within another, the effect encompassed by the cause, like the likeness of these circles, [in] that the greater encompasses the smaller [one] than it, which is the effect. And therefore Keter encompasses Chokhmah and is its cause; and Chokhmah descends from Keter as much as what is between cause and effect; and Chokhmah is a cause to Binah; and behold, Binah descends from Chokhmah one grade and descends from Keter two grades, for it is an effect of this [one] that is an effect of it [Keter]; and in this manner is the descent of the grades down to Malkhut.

Now Malkhut is the end of Atzilut and the head of Beriah; and it [stands] to Beriah as the Ein Sof [stands] to Atzilut; and the last grade in Beriah [stands] to Yetzirah as Malkhut [stands] to Beriah. And this is their order, until they come to the spheres, by way of grades hidden and concealed from us, and revealed to those expert in the account of Creation and the account of the Chariot.

Now there is no distinction between Malkhut and Beriah except like the distinction between cause and effect; and in the descent from the last grade in Atzilut, it was necessitated that the beginning of Beriah — which is the grade that unites with Atzilut, like the union of the effect with its cause — [come to be]; and likewise from Beriah to Yetzirah, and likewise from Yetzirah to Asiyah, down to the spheres.

Now the order of the spheres: the astronomers, [being] blind of eye, imagined that the sphere is adjacent to its fellow, [such] that no space passes between them. But this is not the view of the masters of the Torah, who behold the light of the world: rather, that between firmament and firmament is a journey of 500 years; and although this air is between them, even so the matter indicates the equalization of creation and the necessity, and that it is impossible for there to be, between sphere and sphere, less than this — until the matter descends to the element of fire, and the element of fire unites with the element of air, and the element of air unites with the element of water, and the element of water unites with the element of earth, this above that, with no space between them. And now, who shall set a mouth for a man to ask: let there be yet such-and-such grades, or let there be fewer than them by such-and-such; or why did He not create the world larger than this, or smaller than it? — for all this is great foolishness to those who know the order of the grades. And the constitution of the world is according to the most praiseworthy existence possible in the order of the grades, from the highest possible in existence to the lowest possible in existence, whether in limit, or in end, or in corporeality. And behold, if there were not, between Him and the world, the order of the Sefirot, the world would be impossible — on account of its baseness — to be conducted by the Ein Sof, unless the world were to ascend in the spiritual grades, which are the Sefirot; and for this matter He has [already] emanated the Sefirot. And this intent is none other than to reveal the Emanation and the divinity, and not to conceal it. And its revealing is by means of the descents of the grades to the lowest aspect, which they are now [at]. For even this earth — thick and coarse — down to its navel, has grade after grade, down to seven earths, as we shall explain somewhat of this in [the Gate of] the Order of Their Standing, with God's help — contrary to the view of the foolish astronomers, who imagined [they could] give the measure of the earth, and said that a line of 22,000 mil surrounds it round about, and that, were the earth to be made into a sphere, [a line] would pass to the lower side of its face at a thickness of 7,333⅓ mil — and they walk in darkness.

Now we have, in this matter, a received teaching and a great precedent, as we shall write in the name of the Zohar in the aforementioned Gate. And let us return to our matter: that if the world had been created without intermediation — apart from [the fact] that this is impossible, for the reason we explained —

— behold, this would be the concealment of the divinity: when we come to know His greatness from His governance, would we not [then] believe that He is exalted above His world [by] what is, in truth, [the distance] between the cause and its cause? And therefore, so as not to conceal His divinity, He emanated the grades in the way that I explained — for when we now behold Keter, may He be blessed and exalted, and we elevate above it its cause, the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, how greatly will His name be magnified in the eyes of all His creatures!

And so the glorious chapter is completed, and this Gate is concluded. And after, until now, YHVH has blessed us and helped us in all the way that we have gone, we journey to the place that we have known — namely, to inquire whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, with the help of Heaven.
The Third Gate: To Know Whether the Ein Sof Is the Keter:

What is intended in this Gate is to discuss the matter of the perplexity that has fallen among the Kabbalists, [in coming] to know whether the Ein Sof is the Keter itself or other than it. And this is its name, by which they call it: "Whether the Ein Sof Is the Keter."
Chapter One:

Many of the Kabbalists among the people of our nation have been perplexed with a great perplexity, and have fallen into the pit of error, and thought that the supernal Keter is the Ein Sof, and that it is in the number of the ten. And [there are] some of them who said that, since we have ten grades, what need is there for a further emanation? — but rather that the matter of the Emanator with the emanated [beings] is [the] ten. And they [thought to] support themselves from the Mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, which said "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven"; and they said that [its] saying "and not eleven" [means] to say that we should not add further upon ten — but [rather] that the ten are precisely [the count], [including] the Emanator, who is the Ein Sof, the supernal Keter. This is their way — and may their Master forgive them, for this is a matter of cutting [the shoots] and separation; and one who looks at what I explained concerning that Mishnah, in the First Gate, ch.6, will see that, on the contrary, from there [comes] a proof to the opposite.

Now this view is rejected for several reasons. If you wish, [argue] from Scripture; if you wish, [argue] from reason. The [argument from] reason is: that since the Emanator is distinguished from His emanated [beings] in several matters — first, that the emanated [beings] fall under time, and He does not fall under time. And I do not wish to say "time" according to what appears from the plain sense of our words, but the intent is that there was already a time when they were not emanated, as [for instance] before the Emanation. And this is one of the things impossible in the Ein Sof — that there was [ever] an existence in which He did not exist; rather, He is necessary of existence, and He brought time into existence, and not that He is possessed of time, God forbid. And in this matter is understood [the saying] "first, yet there is no beginning to its beginning" — for although we say "first," and every expression "first" indicates that it has a beginning (for it is true that He is first to all that come after Him) — yet the expression "first" indicates the beginning of time. And therefore it said that He is first, and even so there is no beginning to His beginning; and the expression "first" is only to negate that no other preceded Him. And this is what is said in the Tikkunim, "I am first and I am last." And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that ANI (I) is AYIN (Nothing), which is the supernal Keter. And "I" (ani) is Malkhut, which is the end of the Emanation — "its end embedded in its beginning and its beginning in its end" — for AYIN is alef = supernal Keter, yod = Chokhmah, [final] nun = Binah, with the extension of the vav, which is [the] nun, [i.e.] yod upon vav; and the existence of the [final] nun itself is Malkhut, in truth. It is found [that] AYIN comprehends the whole Emanation. And this [is] "I am first" — the secret of the extension and spreading of the Emanation from above to below; and "I am last" is the existence of the returning light, reversing from below to above. And by this is understood the matter of "first and last": for Keter is truly called "first," because it is first to all that come "in the beginning," which is [the emanated and below]; but above it, in the Ein Sof, the expression "first" does not apply. And this is "and before One, what can you count?" — the meaning [being]: Keter is called "one," which is the beginning of the count, which is the number of the ten, in which the whole count is comprehended, and the count's foundation is above, as we explained in the preceding Gate. And it said that "before One" — which is that [which is] prior to it, namely the Ein Sof — "what can you count?", for there applies there neither number, nor speech, nor any necessity at all. And of Him it is said (Job 37:20), "shall it be counted to Him when I speak?" — for number does not apply there. And with this premise is understood the verse (Isaiah 43) in which all the literalists were perplexed: "You are My witnesses, says YHVH, and My servant whom I have chosen, that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He: before Me no God was formed, and after Me there shall be none." And the explanation: "that I am He" — namely Keter, for it is Keter that is truly called "He" (Hu); and to indicate its concealment, the word "Hu" [is] a pronoun for the hidden [third person]. And therefore it said that it is also called "I" (Ani), to indicate that it is the beginning of the Emanation and the end of the Emanation, in the secret of "I am first and I am last," as explained. And it said "before Me no God was formed" — and the word "formed" (notzar) [is] according to its plain sense, whose meaning is "was not emanated"; for the expression "formation" (yetzirah) too serves [to denote] the Emanation, just as the expression "creation" (beri'ah) serves, namely "In the beginning [God] created." And it said: "before Me none was emanated" — for it [Keter] is the head [first] of those that come within the category of the emanated; and it is the end of the whole Emanation, and this is what is said "and after Me there shall be none." And this indicates the strength of the greatness of the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, which indicates His endurance — that He does not fall under time, but, on the contrary, He brought time into existence, and the existence of His non-being cannot be depicted in any manner in the world. And this is one of His many superiorities over His emanated [beings]: that all of them fall under [contingent] existence, [in] that there was already a time when the Ein Sof was without them, as before the Emanation. And many have thought to say that Keter was prior to all — that is, that, although there was no Emanation, it was in existence, and it is a garment to the Emanator forever. And the holders of this view are masters of the shields [formidable scholars]; and the essential necessity that compelled them to this matter is their saying, of blessed memory, in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, "before the world was created, He and His name alone existed" — the meaning [being] that "He and His name" are the Ein Sof and Keter; and they necessitated from this that Keter is prior, and that it is unified with the Emanator and a garment to Him. But this matter is not fitting to be believed. Rather, that the whole Emanation was emanated at one time, and Keter too is among the emanated [beings], as is necessitated from several passages, some of which we shall copy in the Gates, with God's help — and in particular in the Gate of Essence and Vessels, and in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, and the Gate of the Refinements, with God's help. It is found that the Emanator is exalted above His emanated [beings] — for His emanated [beings], their non-being preceded them; which is not so [with] the Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. And behold, [this is] a first distinction. Further, the Emanator is distinguished from the emanated [beings] in that their life depends on another — namely, on the Emanator who gives them life; and He is the source and the light and the effluence to all His emanated [beings] — they are found, all of them, to need Him; whereas the Ein Sof, blessed be He, needs nothing other than Himself, but is the source of life, and life is found from Him, until He is the life of [all] life. And therefore, in some places, Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, called Him by the expression "a light that does not subsist in [another] light," etc. — since He does not depend on life and effluence from the side of another, but is the source of light to all the other luminaries. And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 132b) and in the Zohar [on] Bereshit (22): "Rabbi Shimon opened further and said: 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me.' He said: Companions, hear ancient words that I wish to reveal... What is [the meaning of] what it said, 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me'? Rather, this is the Cause above all the upper ones, that [One] called the Cause of Causes, the Cause [from] among these causes, [such] that none of these causes does any deed until it takes permission from the one above it, as we established above regarding 'let us make man' — 'let us make,' surely, was said of two, [in] that this one said to the one above it... And the one above it does nothing until it takes counsel from its fellow. But the one called the Cause over all the causes, above which there is none and below which there is none equal to it — this is what is written, 'And to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One.' He said: 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me,' that takes counsel from Him, in the manner of the one that said, 'And God said, let us make man.'" Thus far [the Zohar's] words.

Now [Rashbi], peace be upon him, intended, in this holy passage, to exalt this superiority — that the Ein Sof is exalted above His emanated [beings], [in] that they need to take counsel, the lower from the upper, for it [the lower] needs effluence from its cause that emanates upon it; and therefore it says "let us make man" — as if to say, "you emanate, and I will act, and man is found made by the two of us"; and the upper one still needs to be emanated [upon] from its cause, for it too does not have the ability [on its own]. But the Ein Sof, blessed be He, does not need to say to another "let us make," but [says] "I, I am He, and there is no god with Me" — that is, "in assistance with Me" — neither a lower one, for it has none below it equal to it, nor an upper one, for there is no upper one other than it, for it is above all the existents. And it said "the Cause over all the upper ones, the Cause [from] among these causes" — [Rashbi] intended to explain to us that the reason it is called the Cause of Causes is for two reasons. The first: from the expression "ascent" (aliyah), and the intent is that it is above all the upper ones — and the intent is not an ascent of place, God forbid, for nothing enters into [the category of] place in the Emanation, all the more so in the Emanator, but the meaning [is] the existence of an ascent of degree, and spirituality, and ability. And the second meaning is from the expression "cause" (illah) and "reason" (sibbah) — that it is a cause and a reason to all the causes that are in existence.

Now a second distinction has been explained, by which the Ein Sof, the Emanator, blessed be He, is distinguished from the emanated [beings]. Further, a third distinction, and it is: that all the emanated [beings] have a name among the holy Names, which delimits them, by which that Sefirah and that emanated [being] is called — like Ehyeh in Keter, and Yah in Chokhmah, and so for all the rest of the Sefirot, as we explained in the First Gate explicitly. And likewise the four-letter Name comprehends the whole Emanation, as is explained in the Zohar, and we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. This is not so [with] the Ein Sof, the Emanator, blessed be He, who has no name and [vowel-]point by which we can designate Him, nor attribute that would delimit Him; and we have not found for Him a name to designate Him except "necessary of existence." And the explanation: that He is necessary in His existence, because the world is impossible, ever, without a conductor who gives effluence and life to all the existents; and for this reason His existence is necessary. And because there is no name that would delimit Him, therefore we designate Him "necessary of existence," and this name the philosophers attributed to Him. Further, they attributed to Him the name Ein Sof (Without End), and the reason [is] because He has no end and terminus. For the thing delimited by a name has an end; and the divinity, because it has no end, has no name that would delimit it, and therefore we designate it by [the name] Ein Sof.

And further [there is] another explanation: because the inquiry into Him has no end — for it is not in the manner of the other inquiries, which have an end and a settling upon a single conclusion; but the inquiry into the divinity is without end, and therefore there is none who knows in Him any essence at all, except by means of the Sefirot, which reveal somewhat of His greatness — [and] only from His Sefirot and upward; [but] from there [upward] there is no apprehension, on account of the depth of what is apprehended; and therefore they designated Him Ein Sof. Further, they attributed to Him "Cause of Causes," and the intent is that the causes — from which other [things] are caused — are [themselves] caused [by] Him; and therefore He is called "the Cause of [the] causes," since He is a first cause to all the causes in the world: for although they are causes to other caused [things], even so they are all caused [by] Him. And there are [those] who said that the supernal Keter too is called "the Cause of Causes," since it is a cause to all the other causes, which are caused [by] it; which is not so from it [Keter] and below — [in] that Chokhmah is not a cause to all the caused causes, for Keter is the [one] that causes and is not caused [by] Chokhmah, but on the contrary Chokhmah is caused [by] it. And likewise, for this reason, they said that Keter is called "the Cause of Causes," [in] that it is the cause of the causes that are effects of it. However, the Ein Sof is called "the Cause of all causes" and "the Cause over the causes," with the addition of "all," to indicate, concerning the Ein Sof, that it is the cause of all causes — even Keter; which is not so [with] Keter, of which the expression "all causes" does not [rightly] apply (and likewise it lacks the "all"), since there is already a cause and reason of which it is the caused [one] — [in] that Keter is caused [by] the Ein Sof, and the Ein Sof is its cause; and likewise [the expression with "all"] would not be attributed thus to Keter. And these three names — namely, Ein Sof, and "the Cause of all causes," and "the Cause over all causes" — Rashbi attributed to the Emanator, blessed be He, in his books many times; and he likewise attributed to Him other names, such as "the Concealed of the Concealed," and likewise "the Ancient of Ancients," and many like these similar to them; and when the inquirer examines them closely, he will find that they all indicate the concealment, as we explained — that He has no name, nor being, nor designation that would delimit Him. And behold, [this is] a third distinction, by which the Emanator is distinguished from the emanated [beings] — apart from several other distinctions, such as the removal of measure, and limit, and the predicates, and the changes, for all is in His Sefirot; and we shall not prolong [discussion] of them. And let us say that, since the Emanator is exalted and distinguished from His emanated [beings] [to] the utmost of distinction, and is distanced [to] the utmost of distance, then reason gives that it is not fitting for the Emanator to enter into the number of the emanated [beings], God forbid, as those thought who said that He is the Keter. And now let us come to prove [it] from the proofs.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, established from reason that Keter is not the Ein Sof, now we shall come, in this chapter, to nullify this view from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who enlightens the eyes of Israel in this wisdom; and we have from his words several proofs. First, he said in the book of the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 6), and these are his words: "But the Name YHVH is a chariot to its Master, to the supernal Keter. And therefore, 'there is none holy like YHVH' — the Cause over all, hidden and concealed in Keter; and from it His light spread upon YHVH, which is yod = Chokhmah, heh = Binah, vav comprising six Sefirot, heh = Malkhut" — thus far [his words], for our matter. And this is its explanation: YHVH, which is an allusion to nine Sefirot, as he expounds and goes on, is a chariot to its Master, [namely] Keter; and the reason he said "its Master" is because it [Keter] is a father to the whole Emanation, and the whole Emanation is a throne to it. And it said "there is none holy like [koh]" — [this] will be understood with what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in another place, where he said that "there is none holy like koh" [refers] to Keter. And he said that this is the kaf of "koh," which is the kaf of Keter; and the reason for the kaf is that it is two yods, in the secret of "ten, ten the spoon" (asarah asarah ha-kaf); and this is what he said, "and therefore there is none holy [like koh]" — the meaning [being]: because YHVH is a chariot to Keter — [in] that the four-letter Name [has a] yod at the head [beginning], and Adonai [has a] yod at the end — they are two yods, in the secret of direct light and returning light, which is the kaf of Keter — as this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light, with God's help. And because these two lights are a chariot to Keter, which is the cause of the lights [coming] from the side of the Cause of Causes, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, concealed within it — and from it the light spread by means of Keter, in order that there be direct light and returning light — therefore it is called the kaf of Keter, which is two yods. And let the inquirer not hope from us the explanation of this matter, for its essence is in the aforementioned Gate. Thus far the explanation of the passage, in brief.

Now he said explicitly, "the Cause over all, hidden and concealed in Keter" — indicating that the Ein Sof is not the Keter. Further, he wrote in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 124), and these are his words: "It is called YHVH from the side of the supernal Keter, which is closed up like a closed fist (kometz) that is closed — [such] that none knows what soul there is within. And the one that is within is closed up in thought; the Cause of Causes we call it." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that he said at the beginning of his words, above, that in Malkhut is the four-letter Name without [vowel-]point; and according to her nourishment, so is her vocalization. And now he said "from the side of Keter" — the meaning [being]: when she [Malkhut] is nourished from it [Keter], she is called by the name YHVH, which is [the four-letter Name] with the vocalization of kametz (kometz); and the reason [is] "like a kometz that is closed" — the meaning [being]: like [the One that] is closed up in thought, the meaning [being] that even thought is forbidden in [respect of] Him; and He is called by us "the Cause of Causes" — but not that this name delimits Him, for there is no name that would delimit Him, as we explained in the preceding chapter. And the essence of this passage, with all that follows it, is explained at length in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name.
Behold, he explained to us explicitly that the Cause of Causes is hidden and concealed in Keter, and that the Ein Sof is not the Keter itself.

And further, explicitly, in the Tikkunim in another place (Tikkun 70, folio 130), these are his words: "The supernal Keter, although it is primordial light, clear light, refined light, is dark before the Cause of Causes." And the substance of the passage will be explained in the Gate of the Refinements, blessed be God.

Behold, he indicated explicitly that Keter is not the Ein Sof, in his saying that Keter is dark — that is, that its light does not shine at all [by comparison], that it has no power before the Cause of Causes, which is its Emanator. Further, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 112), these are his words: "A unique Lord, ruling over them all, hidden and concealed in Keter." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that above this passage he spoke of the matter of the spiritual life-forces and chariot in the Sefirot, and afterward he said that the Ein Sof — who is called "a unique Lord," as is explained in Sefer Yetzirah — is hidden and concealed in Keter. And the intent is that His divinity is revealed only by means of the sheath of His light and His garment, which is Keter, and by means of it He rides in the rest of the Sefirot.

Behold, he indicated explicitly that Keter is not the Ein Sof. Further, in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Pinchas, folio 243), these are his words: "Because the Cause of Causes is hidden and concealed in this Keter and spread out in the Name YHVH. On Sabbaths and festivals there is no dominion to Samael and the Serpent, nor to all his appointed [forces]; and there is no dominion to Gehinnom — the evil female of Samael and the Serpent — nor to his hosts: all of them are hidden away before the hosts of the King, in the manner that the nations of the world will be hidden away when the Messiah is revealed; this is what is written, 'and they shall come into the caves of the rocks and into the clefts of the crags.'" And its explanation is clear; and from it, it appears with clarity that one cannot say that Keter is the Ein Sof — [the Ra'aya Mehemna] indicates this in saying "the Cause of Causes is hidden and concealed in this Keter." It appears from his words that Keter is a palace for the Cause of Causes.

Now we have several clear proofs and faithful witnesses that Keter is not the Ein Sof, apart from several other proofs besides — and we have not copied them, because we need to copy them in the coming Gates, such as the passage of Elijah, "You are One," etc., which we shall copy in the Gate of Essence and Vessels, ch.5; and some of them we have not seen [fit] to copy at all, on account of the length. Even so, by these proofs the view of those who say that Keter is the Ein Sof is nullified.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, striven to establish, of necessity, that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, but [that] each of them is a matter in its own right — that is, this [one is] Emanator and this [one] emanated — we have seen [fit], in this chapter, to nullify another view, close to the view of the earlier Kabbalists, namely the view of Rabbi Shem Tov in Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, ch.1, who first counted the Sefirot and said that Keter is the first Sefirah, [and] afterward said that Keter is not in the category of the Sefirot. And this is the form of his language, in utmost brevity: "All the Kabbalists agreed to count these ten Sefirot — the first, supernal Keter; the second, Chokhmah, etc.; however, the most wondrous and the deepest in the wisdom agreed that, in truth, the supernal Keter is not to be counted in the category of the ten, for it is like the Ein Sof; and just as the Cause of all causes is not to be counted at all, so it is not fitting to count the supernal Keter, for there is no beginning and no terminus and end in it, and it is the All. And Rashbi warned about this in several places, and to this he directed [his words] in Sefer Yetzirah, 'ten and not eleven.' And you already know that it is agreed among the sages of the Mishnah that Elijah the prophet is revealed to all the worthy; and there is a tradition, to some of the later [authorities] of blessed memory, that he was revealed to the great Rabbi Abraham, the pious Av Beit Din, of blessed memory, and from him the great Rabbi Ra'avad, his son-in-law, received [it], and the pious Rabbi Isaac, whose tradition is choice flour, [penetrating] very deep into the wisdom of Kabbalah. And he too explained 'ten and not eleven' — that Keter is not to be brought into the count; and the one that completes the count is the supernal Da'at, which the verse alluded to (Proverbs 3:20), 'by His knowledge the depths were cleaved.' And of it [Sefer] ha-Bahir said that it is the holy palace. And the essence of the unique Name written in the books of the Prophets, they directed [it] in the letters of the Name, by means of Tiferet, to this [Da'at], for it is a palace to the supernal root." Thus far [his words].

And he prolonged much further according to this view. And in another place he wrote that, for this reason, Sefer Yetzirah called Chokhmah "the depth of beginning," for it is the beginning, etc. This is the view of Rabbi Shem Tov, who wished to say that Keter is not in the count of the Sefirot — though he admitted, regarding the matter, that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, as is proved from his language in which he said, "and just as the Cause of all causes is not to be counted at all, so it is not fitting to count the supernal Keter" — [thereby] indicating that the Cause of all causes is not the Keter, but [rather] Keter is emanated from it. And before we enter into the demolition of this view, it is fitting that we know who brought them into this error; and we say that they were driven to this view on account of three things. First, the passage "By ten utterances the world was created" (Avot 5:1), which we copied in the preceding Gate, in ch.3; and there we strove with the matter and established that from that passage there is no proof for his words at all. And the second: that they saw [that] in Sefer Yetzirah [the author] began to count from the mishnah of the depths from Chokhmah, in his saying "the depth of beginning and the depth of end," which are Chokhmah and Binah — so that it appears that it [Chokhmah] is first to the Emanation, and Keter is not in the count of the Sefirot; and likewise in his saying "one: the spirit of the living God," etc., "two: spirit from spirit" — they said that "one: the spirit of the living God" is Chokhmah, and "spirit from spirit" is Binah, etc. — [so that] it appears that the count of the ten Sefirot begins from Chokhmah. And the third: that they found a great tree on which to hang, namely the divine Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Idra, [where] these are his words: "The place where the beginning is found is from the Holy Ancient One, which is illumined from the mazal," etc., as we shall copy, with God's help.

Now, since the beginning of the Emanation is from Chokhmah, which is illumined from Keter, it appears explicitly that Keter is not in the category of the count of the ten Sefirot; therefore they pressed themselves to seek the completion of the count of the ten, and sought Da'at. But in truth they did not seek what is right. For the matter of this view is rejected — if you wish, [argue] from Scripture; and if you wish, [argue] from reason. A proof from reason: because [Keter] cannot escape [being one] of two things — either it is emanated, or it is not emanated. If it is emanated, then, since it is an effect of the First Cause, why should it not enter into the count of the Sefirot? For who diminished the honor of the Emanation [so much] that Keter, because it is like the Ein Sof and is great and praiseworthy, should not enter into the count of the Sefirot? — for the Sefirot (namely Chokhmah and Binah) are also like the Ein Sof in their power and their excellence, and even so we did not restrain ourselves from counting them among the ten. And behold, since Keter is a cause to Chokhmah, and Chokhmah a cause to Binah, and the three of them are surely emanated — then as Chokhmah [stands] to Binah, so Keter [stands] to Chokhmah; and just as Chokhmah is counted in the count of the Sefirot together with Binah, so Keter should be counted together with Chokhmah. If so, what is the reason that we should elevate Keter above all the rest of the emanated [beings]? And further, that which he said — that it is like the Ein Sof — is no excellence at all, since it is impossible for it to be exactly equal to the Emanator, for, being an effect of Him, it necessarily descended from the degree of its cause; and after we have exalted the Cause of all causes as much as is possible in [what is] without end, it is not fitting to exalt Keter so much, for it is not at the degree of its Emanator, since it is emanated and an effect of a First Cause, as explained. And as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in saying "it is dark before the Cause of Causes" — he indicated that it is not at the degree of the Ein Sof, God forbid; and if so, why is it "like the Ein Sof"? For the definition of the Ein Sof is a predicate by which nothing is [truly] predicated at all, except [of] the Emanator.
