And since it [Keter] is in the category of the emanated [beings] and is not like the Ein Sof, then why should it not come into the count of the Sefirot? — for it is only of the count of the emanated [beings]; and why should we count some of them and leave out some? This is not fitting. And if you say that it is not emanated — this is impossible to believe, unless we say that it is the Cause of all causes and there is none besides it; for if not so, it is a duality, God forbid, [for us] to say that there is one thing besides the Cause of all causes that was not emanated from it. And if we say that it is emanated as well, but [that] it is not like the rest of the emanated [beings] because it preceded them by a long time — this is impossible, for there cannot be priority over Chokhmah except the priority of cause and effect; for it is impossible to separate and distinguish between every emanated [being] and emanated [being] except like the distinction of cause and effect; and so too the distinction between Chokhmah and Binah. And just as we bring into the count of the emanated [beings] Chokhmah together with Binah, so we also bring in Keter together with Chokhmah. And since, from reason, it is necessitated that Keter is in the count of the ten, it is likewise necessitated from the proof from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 118), [where] these are his words: "And these limbs are all in the Sefirot: the head [is] Keter; the brain, Chokhmah; Binah [is] the heart, and in it 'the heart understands'; the two arms, Chesed and Gevurah; the body, the central pillar; the two thighs, Netzach and Hod; Yesod [is] the member (amah); the Shekhinah [is] its sign (ot)." Thus far [his words].
And although there is somewhat in it to rouse [discussion], even so it is not of [what is] relevant to us.

Now he counted ten Sefirot against the limbs, and counted the supernal Keter [as] the head, and did not count Da'at at all — thus the supernal Keter is in the category of the Sefirot. Further, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3): "And I heard the sound of their wings, in ten kinds of praise. In a simple song, which is yod — Keter; a doubled song, which is YH — Chokhmah and Binah; a tripled [song] in YHV — which is ChaGaT [Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferet]; a quadrupled [song] in YHVH — which is NHYM [Netzach-Hod-Yesod-Malkhut]." Thus far [his words].

Behold, he counted ten Sefirot in ten letters, and did not count Da'at at all, but [rather] Keter. And there is no reason to say that this Keter that he counted is Da'at — for if so, he should have begun from Chokhmah, which is the beginning of the Emanation according to their view; and further, [because] all agree that this one's name is Keter and this one's name is Da'at, and they differ only [as to] which of them comes into the count of the ten.

And further, a proof from the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (folio 31), [where] these are his words: "And therefore 'Bereshit' — bet [+] reshit — is Chokhmah, as Yonatan rendered 'Bereshit' [as] 'with wisdom' (be-chokhmeta), because it is second to the count. And it is called 'reshit' (beginning); [yet] this supernal Keter, [being] concealed, is first; and because it does not enter into the count, the second is [called] 'reshit' — therefore, bet [+] reshit." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that he found a difficulty in the word "Bereshit," for the bet is large, and it alludes to Chokhmah, as is known, and the word "reshit" too alludes to Chokhmah — it is found, then, that Chokhmah is alluded to in this word twice, improperly; and this he intended in saying "Bereshit — bet [+] reshit — is Chokhmah," the meaning [being] that both allude to Chokhmah: the bet, as is well known that it is bet, and "reshit" in his saying "reshit," which is Chokhmah. And because, from this difficulty, I might have said that "Bereshit" in its entirety alludes to Chokhmah — that is, that there is no allusion to Chokhmah for the word "reshit" unless it comes with a bet, namely "Bereshit" — [therefore] he established that the word "reshit" alone is the allusion to Chokhmah; and a proof of this [is] from the Targum of Yonatan, who rendered "be-chokhmeta" and did not say "chokhmeta" — as it appears that the bet always alludes to Chokhmah, apart from the word "reshit," which is also an allusion to Chokhmah, as Yonatan rendered "be-chokhmeta," the bet [being] a servile [prefix].

Now from the Targum of Yonatan it is necessitated that it is always a doubling, for "reshit" is "chokhmeta" and the bet too alludes to Chokhmah. And he answered to the matter of the doubling: because the word "reshit" indicates "beginning," and it would appear that Chokhmah is the beginning of the Emanation and its first [point] — and this is not so, for Keter is the beginning of the Emanation; therefore [the word] came with the letter bet at its beginning, as if to say: although it is called "reshit," even so it is second, by the count of the Sefirot, and Keter is the first. And this is what is said, "because it is second to the count" — the meaning [being]: Chokhmah is second to the count of the Sefirot. "And it is called reshit" — the meaning [being]: and why is it called "reshit," which is, in truth, the place of error, [given] that Keter is the first and the prior? (And therefore he needed to say "bet," as he concludes at the end of his words.) To this he said, "this supernal Keter, [being] concealed, is first" — the meaning [being]: because he found a difficulty [in] that, since in truth it [Chokhmah] is second and not first, then why is it called "reshit," [when] it is not first, since Keter precedes it? And to this he said that Keter is concealed and hidden, and it is not fitting that it be called "reshit"; for the meaning of "reshit" is the beginning of revelation, and the beginning of revelation is in Chokhmah, not in Keter, as will be explained, with God's help. Therefore Chokhmah is called "reshit," and not Keter. And although it is not fitting for Keter to be called "reshit," even so it is first to the Emanation and enters into the count of the Emanation — and this is what is said, "it is first." "And because it does not enter into the count" [the meaning being: into the category of the revealed], as explained, "the second is [called] reshit" — the meaning [being]: it [Chokhmah] is the second, although it is called "reshit," for the reason we explained. "Therefore, bet [+] reshit" — the meaning [being]: and therefore the word "reshit" came doubled, to tell you [that] Chokhmah is called "reshit," and [that] although it is "reshit" it is second — and this is the bet at the head of the word. Thus far the explanation of the passage.

Now he has indicated to us explicitly that Keter is in the count of the ten Sefirot, and that there is no doubt in it, even though Chokhmah is called "reshit." And we have yet very many good proofs, the like of these and these; and we shall not trouble ourselves with copying them here, since we are obliged to copy them in the coming Gates, with God's help.
Now we have established explicitly that Keter is of the count of the Sefirot. (See in [the commentary] Pelach ha-Rimmon.)

Since, in the preceding chapter, we established that Keter is in the count of the Sefirot, it remains for us to explain the matter of the passages that, on their face, oppose this view — namely, those from which the commentators drew a necessity for their view. First, from Sefer Yetzirah, which said in the mishnah of the depths, [where] these are its words: "Ten Sefirot of belimah; their measure is ten, which have no end: the depth of beginning and the depth of end, the depth of good and the depth of evil, the depth of above and the depth of below, the depth of east and the depth of west, the depth of north and the depth of south. And a unique Lord, God, faithful King, ruling over them all from His holy abode for ever and ever." Thus far [its words].

And they said that, since the depth of beginning is Chokhmah and the depth of end is Binah, as they explained, then it is necessitated that the count of the Sefirot is specifically from Chokhmah and below, and that Keter is not in the count of the Sefirot, and [that] the "depth of above" mentioned in the mishnah is Da'at.

And further, they added to bring a proof from another mishnah like this one in Sefer Yetzirah, [where] these are its words: "Ten Sefirot of belimah. One: the spirit of the living God, blessed and praised be the name of the Life of the worlds — voice, and spirit, and speech; and this is the holy spirit. Two: spirit from spirit; He hewed and engraved in it twenty-two letters — three mothers, and seven doubles, and twelve simples — and a [single] spirit [is] in each one of them. Three: water from spirit; He engraved and hewed in them formlessness and void, mire and clay; He engraved them like a kind of garden-bed, and set them up like a kind of wall, and covered them like a kind of ceiling. Four: fire from water; He engraved and hewed in it the throne of glory, and the ophanim, and the seraphim, and the holy living-creatures, and the ministering angels; and from the three of them He founded His abode, as it is said (Psalms 104:4), 'who makes His angels [of] winds, His ministers a flaming fire.' Five: He sealed [the] height; He chose three letters from the simples and fixed them in His great Name, YHV, and sealed with them six extremities; He turned upward and sealed it with YHV. Six: He sealed [the] depth-below; He turned downward and sealed it with YVH. Seven: He sealed [the] east; He turned before Him and sealed it with HYV. Eight: He sealed [the] west; He turned behind Him and sealed it with HVY. Nine: He sealed [the] south; He turned to His right and sealed it with VYH. Ten: He sealed [the] north; He turned to His left and sealed it with VHY. These [are] ten Sefirot of belimah: the spirit of the living God; and spirit; and water; and fire; and height-above, and below, east, west, north, south." Thus far [its words].

Behold, it appears explicitly that [the author] took the path of the other mishnah, and said: "one: the spirit of the living God," which is Chokhmah; and "two: spirit," which is Binah; "three: water from spirit," which is Chesed; "four: fire," which is Gevurah; and "height" is necessarily Da'at — thus necessarily the count of the Sefirot is only from Chokhmah. This is the view of Rabbi Shem Tov, and his [argument from] necessity. And now we are surely obliged to explain these mishnayot, so that all may be rectified, blessed be God. First our occupation will be with the mishnah of the depths, and from there the matter of the preceding mishnah will be explained. And on this mishnah Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote, "I do not understand this clause." Thus far [his words].

And in truth, the difficulty of this mishnah is not so [great] — unless we say that the order was difficult for him. And even so, the humility of the pious one [Ramban], peace be upon him, appears from this: that he chose to say "I do not understand" rather than to demolish the reasoning of his received tradition on account of the difficulty of a single mishnah — because he wished to suspect his [own] view, and not to demolish the boundary of the early [authorities]. And even so, we see no difficulty in this mishnah at all. And this is its explanation: "Ten Sefirot of belimah" — the meaning: this word is divided into two, that is, "beli mah," and the meaning of "mah" is "quiddity" (mahut); and the intent is that the ten Sefirot are without quiddity, since their quiddity is not apprehended by us. And even if we say "this is judgment and this is mercy" and the like, all is apprehended by us [only] from their action, but from their essence they are belimah. Further, it is from the expression "muzzling," as it is written (Psalms 32:9), "with bit (beli) to muzzle" — that it is fitting for a person to muzzle his mouth and not multiply his words about their quiddity and their matter, on account of the shortness of the apprehender and the depth of what is apprehended. Or it is from the expression of concealment and hiding, like "with [adornment] to muzzle," namely the covering of the adornment and its concealment.

Now the Sefirot are called belimah — that is, the Sefirot of concealment, [in] that they are concealed. And these three explanations rise to one place: that the intent is to indicate their concealment and the shortness of [their] apprehension, and that it is not fitting to prolong speech about them on account of their concealment. And it said "their measure is ten"; and because from this it would follow that they have a limit, God forbid, [therefore] it said "which have no end." And although this is a thing and its opposite — that we set a limit in it and afterward say that they have no limit — it has already been explained in the preceding chapters that, in respect of the aspect that they have toward the Emanator, they have no limit, but in respect of their aspect and their action that proceed toward us, they have a limit to their action, according to our reception, [in] that we are possessors of limit. And this is the great power of our Fashioner: without limit, He limits and contracts (tzimtzum) it for the benefit of the lower [beings], who are possessors of limit and end. And at this matter let not the eye of the enlightened be alarmed, for it is not far[-fetched]: for the heavens and the heavens of heavens cannot contain Him, [how much more] blessed be He — and even so, for the love of Israel, He would contract His Shekhinah between the two staves of the Ark, as our Sages of blessed memory explained. "The depth of beginning and the depth of end" are Chokhmah and Binah — for Chokhmah is called "beginning," as is explained in the preceding chapter, and Binah is called "end," for there [is] the end and the conclusion of the things, in the secret of the Jubilee; and this [is] the beginning of the concealment and this [is] its end, in the secret of the transmigration and the Jubilee, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And the reason it said "depth" for each one [is] to indicate that, although "beginning" and "end" and "east" and the rest of the boundaries indicate the limit, even so they are deep — "deep, deep, who can find it?" — and the apprehension of them is precluded, because they are without limit, as explained. And "good" and "evil" are Gedulah and Gevurah, and are called "good" and "evil" because Chesed performs the action of good and reward, and Gevurah performs the action of judgment and punishment; and even so, the expression "evil" is not precise. And after he explained these four depths, he returned to explain six depths, which are the six extremities — namely, the depth of above and the depth of below, east, west, north, south. And this is the reason for the delaying of Keter until here, to [associate it with] the [account of the] extremities — although it is not [properly] associated in [respect of] the matter of the order of the Sefirot; for close to this matter the commentators need to explain, according to their view, that "above" (rom) is Da'at — because Da'at is above Gedulah and Gevurah and below Chokhmah and Binah, as is proved by the verses (Exodus 31:3), "and I filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of work," etc.; and further it is written (Proverbs 24:3-4), "by wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established, and by knowledge the chambers are filled" — thus Da'at precedes Chesed and Gevurah. And if so, why did they delay it until after "the depth of evil" and "the depth of good"? Rather, what have they to say [but] that the reason is on account of the order of the extremities? — if so, for us too the delaying of Keter is on account of the order of the extremities.

And further he said "the depth of above and the depth of below": namely, the supernal Keter, which is exalted above all the Emanation; and the depth of below, namely Malkhut, which is beneath all the Emanation. And the depth of east [is] Tiferet. And the depth of west is Yesod, in which all the powers are mingled — the power of judgment, and the power of Chesed, and the power of mercy — and therefore it is called "west" (ma'arav). Or he means [by] the depth of below, Yesod, which is beneath all the Emanation, [since] Malkhut's place is above, were it not for the accusation, as will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, with God's help; and the depth of west [would then be] Malkhut, in which all the powers are mingled.

And further, [Yesod] is always opposite the east. And east and west [are] Tiferet and Malkhut. And the depth of north and the depth of south are Netzach and Hod — for Netzach's inclination is toward Chesed, namely south, and Hod's inclination is toward Gevurah, namely north; and therefore north and south rightly [apply] to them. And "a unique Lord" is the Ein Sof, who is not in the count of the Sefirot, God forbid — the opposite of that view which we nullified in chapter 1 and chapter 2 of this Gate. And as for the reason he said "[God] (El), [faithful] King (melekh ne'eman)" — we may say that [their] initials [are] AMeN [alef-mem-nun]; and AMeN equals 91, like the count of [the combined Name] YAHDVNHY [the interweaving of YHVH and Adonai]. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained many times. And some of the masters of the wisdom attributed this name [Amen] to the Ein Sof — not because the Ein Sof receives a name, God forbid, but because this name indicates the union and the joining to the Sefirot that [occurs] by means of Tiferet and Malkhut, from below to above and from above to below. For the four-letter Name comprehends all the Sefirot from above to below, and Adonai comprehends the ten Sefirot from below to above. And this is [the] yod at the head [beginning], and this is [the] yod at the end, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light, with God's help. Therefore they attributed this name to it, to indicate that this union, alluded to in the [combined] Name YAHDVNHY, is by means of it. And this is [why] he designated it here "[God] (El), [faithful] King (melekh ne'eman)."

And further: the word "El" (God) indicates the necessity of His existence; and "melekh" (King) indicates the existence of His providence and His kingship in the lowly world and in all the worlds; and "ne'eman" (faithful) indicates His eternity and His endurance — that He is faithful [in] that He shall not be moved, God forbid. And this whole matter necessitates the Ein Sof, as we explained somewhat in chapter 1. And it said "ruling over them all" — the meaning: from above to below and from below to above.

And the matter of "ruling over them all" [is] to indicate the essence that spreads within the vessels, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of Essence and Vessels, with God's help. "From His holy abode" — this is Keter, where its [the Ein Sof's] concealment is, as was explained in chapter 2 from [the words of] Rashbi, peace be upon him. "For ever and ever" (ad adei ad) — the meaning: three attributes called "ad," [namely] Binah, Yesod, Malkhut, which comprehend the whole Emanation in general. For Binah comprehends the first three; and Tiferet and Yesod are all one, for "body and covenant we reckon as one"; and this is the vav, which comprehends the six extremities; and Malkhut is itself. Thus, in the matter of "ve-AD ADei AD," the whole Emanation is comprehended. Or it is possible to say "ve-ad adei ad" [means]: although the comings-into-being have spread for ever and ever, even so He rules over them all, whether they grow distant or whether they draw near. Thus far the explanation of the mishnah. And we have answered the matter of its beginning with Chokhmah — for its intent is not, God forbid, that Keter does not enter into the count of the Sefirot, but [that] the "depth of above" is Keter; and if it did not count it in its order, first to all the Sefirot, it is on account of the order of the extremities. And in this manner is the way, and this is the reason, for the mishnah of the seals that we wrote at the beginning of [this] chapter. And it is found that these mishnayot are no necessity at all to overturn the premises that are our received tradition.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, explained the aforementioned mishnah in the way that the commentators explained it — "to show the peoples and the princes its beauty," and [to show] that there is no necessity from it for the words of the commentators at all, even according to their way — now we have seen [fit] to write [in] it what is [further] expounded. And it is written in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 14), [where] these are his words: "Ehyeh is YHV, and it is the sum of six sides, with which He sealed six sides; and they are YHV, HVY, VHY, VYH, HYV, YVH. YHV — He took it [to] the right, which is Chesed, and sealed Chokhmah with it; and with it, 'one who wishes to become wise, let him turn south.' HVY — He took [to] the left, which is Gevurah, and sealed wealth with it; and with it, 'one who wishes to become rich, let him turn north.' VHY — He turned to the east and took the central pillar and sealed 'children' (banai). VYH — He took it [to] the right thigh and looked with it upward and sealed 'life' (chayei) with it. HYV — He took it [to] the left thigh and looked downward and sealed 'sustenance' (mezonei) with it; He looked upward toward Chokhmah and bound [it] to the right thigh and sealed 'life' with it, because of Chokhmah it is said, 'wisdom gives life to its possessors'; He looked upward toward the supernal Imma and bound [it] to the left thigh and sealed 'sustenance' with it. YVH — He turned to the west, to the Tzaddik, which is the mixing (eruv), where all the powers are mingled; and it was included in eighteen (ch"y) letters, which are YHV, HVY, VHY, VYH, HYV, YVH — these are the eighteen (ch"y) letters by which He is called 'Living (ch"y) of worlds,' and the Tzaddik by them is called 'Life (ch"y) of worlds.'" Thus far [his words].

And in truth, at this explanation the enlightened one will be astonished — for the six extremities mentioned are literally six extremities, as is its custom throughout the Zohar; for the six extremities are always the six days of construction, and there are no "extremities" except in the place of construction. And this matter — how good and how pleasant! But the matter of "one," and "two," and "three," and "four" is difficult for them, for there is, on its face, no way to explain them. Further, we have seen, regarding the matter of the mishnah of the depths, that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in this manner — these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 120b), in this matter, [in] the book "These are the generations of Adam" and in the matter of "and you shall envision" — [where] these are his words: "These four letters are clothed in these four colors: yod in a white color, heh in a red color, vav in a green color, heh in a black color. This Name is the one that embroiders colors in every place, and it is the one that depicts the lines of the forehead, in this manner: YHVH; and these [are] the four traced [lines] of the lines, which are the depth of above, and the depth of below, and the depth of east, and the depth of west." Thus far [his words].

Now he indicated that the four depths of the mishnah — which are above, below, east, and west — are four colors, which are white, red, green, black. And in truth, according to what is customary, white and red [are] Chesed and Gevurah. But he did not explain so in the mishnah of the seals, as is proved above; rather, [there] above and below are Netzach and Hod — and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in other places, regarding the verse (Ezekiel 1:27), "from the appearance of His loins and upward" and "from the appearance of His loins and downward," that they are Netzach and Hod. And therefore we may [be] press[ed] to explain that the "depth of above" and "depth of below" mentioned are also Netzach and Hod, and that they too are red and white — although these are not their essential colors, even so they are included in these colors, for this one's inclination is toward the right and this one's toward the left; and with this, the matter of yod and heh — which are the letters clothed in these two colors — is also related to them, as he explained. And he said, "these four letters are clothed in these four colors: yod in a white color, heh in a red color" — in the manner that we said in the preceding passage, in the explanation of the mishnah of the seals, where he said, "He looked upward toward Chokhmah and bound [it] to the right thigh," and likewise Hod, with which Binah is bound — and it is found that the yod is in Netzach and the heh is in Hod, [pointing] to this matter. And now the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the two places, in the two mishnayot, are found according to his way; and from within it there came forth for us a great light regarding the matter under discussion before us. First, he said "one: the spirit of the living God" — it is Keter; and so it is necessitated from what he said, "blessed and praised be His name." And these are his words also in Sefer ha-Bahir, in the Sefirah of Keter, where he said: "And what are the utterances? The first — the supernal Keter, blessed and praised be His name." As it appears that he attributed "blessed and praised be His name" [as] relating to this Sefirah. And the matter is that, although the word "blessed" (barukh) is found alluded to in various places, the essence of its allusion is in Keter. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 116b), [where] these are his words: "For 'in Yah, YHVH, is the rock of worlds'; and it is the bet of 'barukh' (blessed). And the sign: 'barukh' in the initials of [its] letters — resh [=] head (rosh), vav [=] source (makor), kaf [=] all (kol): the blessings (berakhot), [in] that this is the head and the source of all the blessings. And therefore bet — it is Chokhmah and indicates Keter, which is the head and the wellspring of all blessings; and therefore bet is two, by the count." Thus far [his words].

And its essence [is] there, in the matter of the bet of Avgitatz; and he said that it is a head, that it is the name BYHRYRWN (Bihariron). The meaning: "for in Yah, YHVH, is the rock of worlds." And he said that the letter bet of "ba-Yah" (in-Yah) means "barukh." And the matter is that "barukh" [signifies] the head and source of all blessings, namely Keter, which is the source of all the blessings. And therefore the word "ba-Yah" came [with] a bet at its head, to indicate that it [Chokhmah] is second (namely Chokhmah), emanated from the source of the blessings, which is Keter, the first Sefirah. And now let us say that the meaning of "blessed and praised be His name" [is]: it is Keter; it is "blessed" (barukh), whose meaning is the head and source of all the blessings, and it blesses and emanates to Chokhmah, which is the name of Keter. For the definition of "name" means a garment and covering, as will be explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, with God's help; and the garment and covering of Keter is Chokhmah. And the meaning of "one: the spirit of the living God": the meaning [of] "one" [is] that it is a soul and a vital spirit to Chokhmah, which is "the living God" (Elohim Chayim); and it is called so, because from Chokhmah the source of life flows. And Keter is called "one," for so he alluded: "one," "one and one" — they are the first three, as is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places. "Blessed and praised be the name of the Life of the worlds" — I have already explained that this is expounded of Keter; and it is called "the Life of the worlds" because Keter is the life of all the existents, since it is the source of all the blessings entirely. "Voice, and spirit, and speech," etc. — the meaning, in the matter that it is called "the Life of the worlds": the meaning [of] "the worlds" [is] the worlds standing concealed in Chokhmah, where its [Keter's] effluence is; for the worlds revealed from Chokhmah and below, although they are nourished by means of Keter, [it is] by means of intermediaries; but when these worlds are in Chokhmah, then in truth they are nourished from it — from Keter specifically. And this is "voice, and spirit, and speech" — the meaning [of] the worlds of which Keter is called their life. And this is what he said, "voice," namely Tiferet, which comprehends the six extremities; "and spirit" is "a voice that is not heard," which is the still small voice, namely Binah, which is a spirit that has no sound, but [is] "a voice that is not heard," as explained, namely Binah; "and speech" is Malkhut. And this is "the holy spirit" — the meaning [being] that the sum of these three is [the place] where they are nourished from Keter; and then it is called "blessed" and the source of blessings and "the Life of the worlds," namely these three letters, which are HVH concealed in the yod. "Two: spirit from spirit; He hewed and engraved in it" — the meaning [of] "in it" [is]: with it, namely, by the power of Chokhmah He engraved and emanated effluence, so that the letters would be depicted in Binah, namely the twenty-two letters. Or we may say "in it" literally, in its plain sense; and the reason [is] that the matter in which the supernal forms were depicted is the thirty-two paths, and they were the matter and the thickening of the earth in which the twenty-two letters were cast — namely the three mothers, which are AMaSh, which are KaChaB [Keter-Chokhmah-Binah], or we may say Ch[okhmah]-B[inah]-and-Da'at. And according to all the explanations, AMaSh — its matter is the letters YHV, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light. And it is known that the existence of the vav in Keter is the secret of Da'at, as this will be explained, with God's help. And now "in it" — in Chokhmah, literally — is the existence of the depiction of Ch[okhmah]-B[inah]-and-Da'at; and therefore the creation of the world was in ChaBaD, namely the thirty-two paths of Chokhmah; and all is one, unified. "Seven doubles" are the seven Sefirot of construction, which are double, composite of judgment and mercy, the allusion to which is in BeGeD KeFeReT, which receive dagesh — namely judgment — and rafe — namely mercy. "And twelve simples" are the twelve diagonal boundaries, which will be explained at length in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names, with God's help.

And the matter of three and seven and twelve will be explained yet further in the Gate of Existence, with God's help. "And a spirit [is] in each one" — the meaning: when He emanated the letters, there was emanated from the essence of Chokhmah a spirit and a soul to each one of them, namely the vocalization, which is a soul to the letters — the letters [being] in Binah and the vocalization from Chokhmah. And in the Sefirot, "a spirit in each one of them" [is] the essence that spreads within the vessels, for such was the [mode of] existence of their emanation, as will be explained from the passage of the Zohar in the Gate of Essence and Vessels, in ch.7. "Three: water from spirit" is Binah, which is third. [The meaning [of] "water" (literally) — as is written in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation, ch.4 — [is] in the matter of the third utterance, which is "let the waters be gathered," [and] is in Binah. And the reason it is called "water" is because they are thicker than the spirit, and they receive the depiction more; and likewise it [Binah] receives more the depiction of the existents, and there they are revealed more than in Chokhmah.] "He engraved in them formlessness and void, and mire and clay," which are the existence of the four letters that are in Binah: formlessness (tohu) [is] yod, void (bohu) [is] heh, vav [is] mire (refesh), heh [is] clay (tit). And in [Genesis] Rabbah it explained: what is "bohu"? — a thing that clothes the tohu. And it said [that] tohu is "a green line that encircles the world," which is Binah — and not Binah itself, but the yod that is in Binah, which has a hylic existence that is not revealed in essence — that is, that the intellect judges in it all judgments, in the manner of the hyle (prime matter), and it bears them, on account of its great distance from [human] knowledge [to apprehend]; but "bohu," which is the heh, clothes the yod, namely heh, a house and a palace to the yod, like this:

And it is "bohu" that gives depiction to the tohu and reveals the matters concealed in it. "Mire" (refesh) is a greater thickness, indicating greater revelation; and this is "mire," which is the vav, which is Tiferet, which is the revelation of Binah, although it is still concealed in it. And "clay" (tit) is [a still] greater thickness and revelation, namely Malkhut, which is the final heh.

Now the [mode of] existence of their emanation in Binah is from the power of Chokhmah. "He engraved them like a kind of garden-bed," etc. — here he included the existence of the six extremities: namely, "like a kind of garden-bed" is the below; "and set them up like a kind of wall" is the girding of the four walls of the wall — west, east, north, south; "covered them like a kind of ceiling" is the above — to indicate that, in the existence of the vav stated in the word "mire" (refesh), as I explained there, the six extremities mentioned are included, and they are in the power of Binah. "Four: fire from water," etc. — it is Malkhut; and by means of it the rest of the worlds were created, for by means of the first three all the Emanation was made and emanated, and in particular by means of Binah. And he placed Malkhut first [with the word "clay"], before the existence of the [other] extremities, because they were already alluded to in their existence within Binah. And because he mentioned their emanation from Binah, he mentioned the rest of the existence of the worlds, namely the throne of glory and the seraphim, etc. And Malkhut is called "fire" because it is the lower Gevurah; and he said "from water," [in] that it is Malkhut from Binah, and so [is] their inclination: Binah, the upper heh, its inclination is toward the right, and Malkhut, the lower heh, its inclination is toward the left, and they are the right hand and the left hand, as is proved in the Tikkunim, and as will be explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, with God's help. And the secret of the throne of glory is Beriah, as we shall explain in the Gate of ABY"A. "And from the three of them He founded His abode" — the meaning: from these three aspects, which are spirit, water, fire, are the foundation and the abode of the Shekhinah, as is proved by the verses. "Five: He sealed [the] height," etc. — namely Netzach, namely above. And he placed it first for [several] reasons: either because the essence of its sealing was by means of Chokhmah, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, as we set down earlier; and likewise the sealing of the below, which is Hod, was by means of Binah, and therefore he placed it first; or for the sake of the order of the extremities. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, was compelled, in the passage of the Tikkunim, to explain that the sealing of above and below was by means of Chokhmah and Binah, because with them were sealed "life" (chayei) and "sustenance" (mezonei); and we hold that "children, life, and sustenance" depend not on merit (zekhut) — namely Chesed — but on mazal — namely Keter; and not Keter specifically, but the first three. And so it is proved in the Zohar in Parashat Vayera, on the verse "behold, I [will] add to your days" — that it did not say "I am adding" (mosif), speaking in the present[, addressed] to [the listener's] presence, but "I will add" (yosif), speaking of the hidden [third person], which is Binah. Therefore, surely, the mazal — although its essence is Keter — is in partnership with the first [three]; and therefore, in order to seal "life" and "sustenance" in Netzach and Hod, it was necessitated [that it be] by means of Chokhmah and Binah. And by this is understood the doubled language of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the passage [mentioned above]. "Seven: He sealed [the] east," etc.; "Eight: He sealed [the] west," etc. — namely Tiferet and Yesod, as explained in the preceding chapter, and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And north and south [are] according to their plain sense, which are GaG [Gedulah-Gevurah]. And after we have included the explanation of the mishnah of the seals, let us explain the mishnah of the depths; and this is its explanation, in this manner, and not exactly like it: "the depth of beginning and the depth of end" are Keter and Malkhut, in the secret of "I am first and I am last," which we explained in chapter 1. "The depth of good and the depth of evil" are Chokhmah and Binah, for this is the source of mercy and Chesed, as is known, and this is the source of judgment and punishment; and according to all the explanations, "evil" is not precise. And "the depth of above and the depth of below," etc., are the six extremities, as I explained above. And we have gained, by the way, that these six extremities are literally the six sides mentioned, and [are] alluded to in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places; and there is nothing twisted or crooked in them, and "each man comes to his place in peace." And their proof from these mishnayot is nullified, [in] that "the pendants that were leaning [on it] are washed away." And in the way that he explained in the Tikkunim, he likewise explained in the Ra'aya Mehemna, in the completion of the ten emendations of the table; and we have not seen [fit] to copy it here, so as not to be lengthy.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, striven in the explanation of the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah and to nullify the proofs of Rabbi Shem Tov and the rest of the commentators who say that Keter does not enter into the count of the Sefirot, we shall now come, in this chapter as well, to nullify his proof from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (in the Idra of Ha'azinu, folio 289b), [where] these are his words: "The place where the beginning is found is from the Holy Ancient One, which is illumined from the mazal — it is the illumination of Chokhmah, which spreads to thirty-two directions; and they came forth from that concealed brain, from the illumination that is in it. And what the Holy Ancient One illumines first (a variant: in Chokhmah) — this it is; and the beginning was from what was revealed; and it was made into three heads, and one head includes them. And these three spread out in Zeir Anpin, and from these all is illumined. This Chokhmah was engraved, and it brought forth one river that flows and issues to water the garden; and it entered the head of Zeir Anpin, and was made into one brain; and from there it is drawn and flows into the whole body, and waters all those plantings; this is what is written, 'and a river issues from Eden [to water the garden,' etc. Again,] this Chokhmah was engraved and was drawn, and entered the head of Zeir Anpin, and was made into another brain. That illumination which was drawn from it — these two drawings were engraved and joined as one by means of [one] drawing of the depth of the well, of which it is written, 'by His knowledge the depths were cleaved'; and it entered the head of Zeir Anpin and was made into another brain; and from there it is drawn and enters within the body, and fills all those chambers and halls of the body; this is what is written, 'and by knowledge the chambers are filled.' And these are illumined from the illumination of that supernal, concealed brain that is illumined by the mazal of the Holy Ancient One; and all are suspended this from that, and bound this to that and that to that — until it is recognized that all is one, and all is the Ancient One, and nothing is separated from it. These three lights illumine three others, which are called the fathers; and these fathers illumine the sons; and all is illumined from one place." Thus far [his words].

And regarding this passage, there has come to us a certain treatise (kuntres) from one of the accepted sages of this generation, and he explained in it an interpretation at length, with proofs from passages of the Zohar. And since, afterward, he returned and explained the construal of the language of the passage and its explanation without [bringing] proofs to his premises, we have seen [fit] to copy here that [shorter] interpretation, so that the examiner may be wary of it — for we shall not need to be lengthy, since most of our premises are explained in these Gates. And these are his words: "'The place where the beginning is found' — the place of the beginning of the Emanation, which is found and emanated from the Holy Ancient One, the Ein Sof, which illumines by way of Keter, called 'mazal' — and the reason you will find in the long explanation. 'It is the illumination of Chokhmah' — it is the light of Chokhmah, the wisdom of God, whose light spreads in the thirty-two paths. 'And they came forth,' etc. — that the spreading of this light comes and issues from Keter, called the supernal Keter, sealed and concealed, and does not fall under thought. 'And what the Holy Ancient One illumines,' etc. — and what the Ein Sof illumines first. 'This it is' — that is, Chokhmah. 'And the beginning was from what was revealed,' etc. — and the beginning of the revelation of the Emanation from the Ein Sof is this [Chokhmah], for Keter is not apprehended even in thought. 'And it was made into three heads' — this Emanation that comes from the Ein Sof was made [into] three heads, [which] are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. 'And one head includes them' — for although they have [their separate] place, the true union is only in [all] three of them. 'And these three spread out in Zeir Anpin' — the three mentioned spread their emanation down to the last [Sefirah], called Zeir Anpin; and the matter, [see the long explanation]. 'And from these all is illumined' — all of them receive these light and effluence, and they have none besides them. 'This Chokhmah was engraved' — the meaning of what he said above, 'and three heads were made': for we found only two, and the third — how was it emanated? He said, 'it was engraved,' etc. — this [Chokhmah] was opened and there was emanated from it [the third]. 'An illumination that flows and issues' — it is Binah; and the reason it is called so, [see the long explanation]. 'These two' — they are Chokhmah and Binah, which were emanated and drawn from Keter, [and which] open and draw themselves together in one drawing into the depth of Tiferet, into all those chambers and halls; and the matter of the drawing of this light from Chokhmah and Binah, [see the long explanation]. 'And these illumine with illumination' — these chambers all illumine with the light of that attribute, which is Keter, the mazal of the Holy Ancient One. 'And all are suspended this from that' — and all the Sefirot are bound this to that, until the Emanation that comes from the Ein Sof is recognized and known and apprehended; and this matter is a great secret among the secrets of the Kabbalah, and the matter you will understand, [see the long explanation]. 'And all is one' — and all is unified, this unifying with that. 'And all is the Ancient One' — and all of them are unified in it like a flame bound to a coal. 'These three lights' — they are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. 'Illumine three others' — they are Chesed, Pachad, Tiferet, which, below them, are unified each one opposite [the upper] one: Chesed in Chokhmah, and Pachad in Binah, and Tiferet ascends by way of the middle line and is unified in Keter; and the reason, [see the long explanation]. 'And these fathers illumine the sons' — they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and [the reason] he called these 'fathers' and these 'sons,' [see the long explanation]. 'And all is illumined from the place of the beginning' — he now returned and included all that he said above, and concluded with that with which he began: all the Sefirot receive their light from the place of the beginning of the Emanation." Thus far the short interpretation. And in every place where "TBH" (tav-bet-heh) is written [in his text], its initials [mean] "you will find it in the long explanation," since there he brought a passage or passages from the Zohar as proof for that matter; and these passages neither raise nor lower [anything] in the explanation of the passage at all. And what there is to object to him is this: that he explained "the Holy Ancient One" [as] the Ein Sof — and this does not appear [correct], for even Keter, most of the time, Rashbi, peace be upon him, designates by the name "Ancient of Ancients" (Atika de-Atikin); how much more, then, would he now designate the Ein Sof by the name "Holy Ancient One"?

And further, that it is impossible for the intent of "the Holy Ancient One" to be the Ein Sof, because he [Rashbi] said that the Holy Ancient One is illumined and receives its light from the mazal — and therefore he said "is illumined" (de-itnehir) in the passive form, and did not say "illumines" (de-anhir) or "illumines" (de-nahir), which is an active verb; and so it is written in all the versions, and so it was written in the version of this commentator [too] — and even so, he pressed to explain it [in] the active form, [in] that he said "the Holy Ancient One, the Ein Sof, which illumines by way of Keter, called mazal." Thus far [his words].

And further, his saying is difficult: "and what the Holy Ancient One illumines first — this it is." And he explained: "that which the Ein Sof illumines first is this," that is, Chokhmah. And it is difficult — for, granted, "'and the beginning was from what was revealed,' etc." is fine, for although it [Chokhmah] is second to the Emanation, even so it is first to the revelation; but "'and what the Holy Ancient One illumines,' etc." appears [to mean] that this is literally the beginning of its illumination — and this is not so, for Keter is the beginning of illumination and Emanation according to all the explanations, even according to the words of Rabbi Shem Tov; for, certainly, they differ only [in] that he says it is not fitting that Keter enter into the count, but he admits that it is the beginning of the illumination of the Ein Sof.

And further, the doubled language "and the beginning" does not settle with his interpretation at all. Further, his saying "and it was made into three heads" — for, granted, if he were speaking of the [mode of] existence of the Emanation in general, it would be fine for him to say that this Emanation was made [into] three heads, which are Keter-Chokhmah-Binah; but the intent of the passage was only to say that the [mode of] existence of the beginning of the revelation is Chokhmah — if so, why did he say "it was made into three heads"? For which one was made into three heads? — since the particulars of the heads he mentioned above, [where] he said "which is illumined from the mazal," namely Keter, "it is the illumination of Chokhmah," namely Chokhmah: it is not applicable to it [Chokhmah] [to say] "it was made into three heads." Further, he said "and one head includes," etc. — he explained: that although they have [their separate] place, the true union is only in [all] three of them. And it is difficult — for if the intent were to say that the three of them are reckoned as one, he should not have said "and one head," which implies one Sefirah that includes them, but [rather] "and they are included in one," the intent [being] that the three of them are reckoned as one. Further, he said "and these three spread out in Zeir Anpin," and explained: the three mentioned spread their emanation down to the last [Sefirah], etc. — and this is a great strain, for the nature of the language does not indicate that his occupation here is with the matter of the [mode of] existence of the Emanation; and likewise it would not have been fitting for him to say "and they spread out in Zeir Anpin," which implies that Zeir Anpin is already emanated, whereas according to his interpretation he is still occupied with the beginning of the Emanation, before the whole structure was emanated. And there are yet very many matters with superfluous language, whose matter is not explained according to his interpretation; and so as not to be lengthy, it is not my wish to object to all his words — and with a little examination the difficulty of his understanding in the interpretation will be apprehended. And now it is fitting that we come to the interpretation of the passage in a manner that a settled explanation may be explained, and the proofs of Rabbi Shem Tov nullified, with God's help.

Before we enter into the explanation of this passage, we must preface one premise briefly — and its explanation will be at length in the book Or Yakar, in the commentary on the Idra, with God's help. And the matter is that, although ten Sefirot are emanated, and they are garments to the light of the providence of His governance, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Vessels, with God's help — even so, He clothes Himself in Keter, and there is the palace of His providence and His light; and it [Keter] is what cleaves and unites with the Emanator [to] the utmost [degree of] cleaving and union, to the point that it is forbidden to prolong speech about this matter.

Now, by means of Keter, the concealment of His existence is a first concealment. And accordingly, the concealment of Keter was necessitated, to the point that its existence is not literally revealed in the rest of the Sefirot, nor will it be revealed in them; and just as they are not comprehended of the existence of the Emanator, so they are not comprehended of Keter — except that Keter pours its effluence, by the power of the Emanator, into the Sefirot, by means of Da'at, as will be explained, with God's help. And on account of the great concealment of Keter, we do not call it "the beginning of the Emanation," because it is not the beginning of the Emanation that is revealed to us — but [rather] Chokhmah; and from Chokhmah and below are the totality of the Sefirot, [counted] from ten, by means of the Da'at that completes [the count]. And not that Da'at is a Sefirah — rather, it is an aspect that completes the totality of the Sefirot, [enabling] them to be composed of ten from Chokhmah and below, as we shall expand the explanation in the aforementioned book. And we know that this matter alarms the heart of beginners in the wisdom of Kabbalah, and the things do not settle for them until they come to the place that we have appointed for this inquiry — and then the gates of light will be opened.

Now the emanation of Keter is called Arikh Anpin (the Long Face), and it is the first concealment to the Emanator. The second concealment is Zeir Anpin (the Small Face), and it includes all eight Sefirot, which are from Chokhmah to Yesod; and this is the secret of the second concealment to the Emanator. The third concealment is called Nukva de-Zeir Anpin (the Female of Zeir Anpin), and it is Malkhut. And the secret of these three concealments is explained in the Idra, at the passing of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as the explanation will be expanded for us there. And even so, let these matters be [set] before the examiner; and let him not rebel against them, but let him kiss his lips and say, "if it is a received tradition, we shall receive [it]" — for the place of their explanation we have appointed to the aforementioned book, with God's help.

And further, we must preface a premise that we received from our teacher and master, Rabbi Solomon — may his light shine — that each and every Sefirah is examined in three aspects: the first aspect, in respect of what it receives; the second, in respect of its [own] essence; the third, in respect of what it emanates. The example of this [is] in Chokhmah, which is the matter under discussion before us: it has a first aspect, in respect of which it is equalized to Keter — [and] in this aspect it receives and is illumined from it; and this aspect is its fineness and its spirituality, higher in degree than the aspect of its [own] essence, since the supernal Keter is joined to it. And it has a second aspect, which is the aspect of its [own] essence, which is its [particular] character — which is the light that illumines in its essence, without any other Sefirah besides it being joined to it. And it has a third aspect, which is the aspect in which it is equalized to Binah, in order to emanate to it from its effluence.

Now this aspect is not fine and spiritual like the first two aspects, for the reason that the lower attribute, which is below it, is joined to it. And not specifically Binah — rather, the same applies to Chesed and the rest of the Sefirot that draw sustenance from it.

And further, we must preface, regarding the matter of this passage in general: that this passage was expounded in Parashat Ha'azinu, at the time of the passing of Rashbi, peace be upon him, after he had expansively spoken of the matter of Keter and its concealment, and that upon it depends the whole essence of the Emanation. Afterward he began to speak of the [mode of] existence of the Emanation that is revealed, and said that, from the side that Keter is not revealed, therefore the beginning of all the limbs of the Holy Ancient One — their beginning is Chokhmah; and the matter of the three brains, which are opposite the three supernal [Sefirot], because Keter is concealed, as he explained there. He said, in the totality of this passage, that the [mode of] existence of the three brains included in the Chokhmah that is in Keter are three Sefirot; and its two aspects [those of Chokhmah] come in the place of the two Sefirot, which are Keter and Binah, and the aspect of Da'at that is in Chokhmah is found in the place of Keter itself, as he explains and goes on. And since he came to explain the matter of the three brains that are in Arikh Anpin, by the way he indicated to us the order of the drawing-of-sustenance of the grades — that is, the three fathers, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, draw sustenance from the three brains; for the first of them — that is, the matter of Da'at, as will be explained, and it is in the place of Keter — and from there [is] their sustenance, that is, from these three aspects. And from the three fathers [is] the sustenance of the three branches, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod. And now the matter of the sustenance of the Sefirot, three from three, is understood, although Keter is concealed. And now we shall come to the explanation of the language of the passage, with God's help. "The place where the beginning is found" — the meaning: the place of the revelation of the Emanation and its being found by us; that is, although the beginning of the Emanation is from the supernal Keter, which is Arikh Anpin, even so it is concealed and is not revealed on account of its great concealment, and the beginning of the revelation of the Emanation is from Zeir Anpin, whose beginning is Chokhmah; and it is called "the beginning" (shiruta) because it is the beginning of the revelation. And he said that its emanation and its [mode of] existence, in [terms of] existence, is from Arikh Anpin, which is Keter. And this is what he said, "the place where the beginning is found" — the meaning: the place where Chokhmah is emanated and found and revealed is from the Holy Ancient One, that is, Keter, Arikh Anpin, called the Holy Ancient One. And the expression "Ancient One" (Atika) indicates priority, as he indicated in the verse (Daniel 7:9), "and the Ancient of Days." And it is called "Holy" (Kadisha), for there is the source of all the holinesses; or he means that "holy" (kadosh) means "separate" and "elevated," and it is holy [i.e., separate] in respect of Zeir Anpin, which is emanated in revelation.

And further, because there are two elders — this elder, who has acquired wisdom, and there is, in the Sitra Achra, a worthless elder (zaken ashmai), as is known, in the secret of Laban the Aramean — therefore he called it "the holy elder," the meaning [being]: in the secret of holiness, and in its joy no stranger may mingle. "Which is illumined from the mazal" — the meaning: that this "beginning" of which he spoke does not illumine from the side of the essence of Keter, for it is concealed [to] the utmost concealment, but [rather] from the side of a revealed aspect within it, which is the secret of the beard (dikna) of the Holy Ancient One, the beard of Arikh Anpin, and it is called "mazal." And it is the secret of the aspect of Binah that is in Keter, as will be explained in the aforementioned book. And this aspect in Keter is called by the name "mazal" to indicate the emanating aspect within the supernal Keter — that it emanates by it into Zeir Anpin; for that aspect is called "mazal," from the expression "water shall flow (yizal) from his buckets" (Numbers 24:7), and "and flowing [streams] (nozlim) from Lebanon" (Song of Songs 4:15). And the intent now [is]: although Keter was emanated, the beginning of the revelation of the Emanation is in Chokhmah, in the aspect of its reception from the supernal Keter. And it is found, accordingly, that the aspect of the beard that is in Keter emanates into the first aspect of Zeir Anpin, which is Chokhmah; and this is what is meant in his saying "which is illumined from the mazal." And so [is] the way — for the last aspect of this [Sefirah] emanates into the first [aspect of the next], and the first aspect of Chokhmah is the beginning of the revelation. "It is the illumination of Chokhmah, which spread to the thirty-two directions" — before its interpretation, we must preface that there are two Chokhmahs, and of them it is said (Proverbs 1:20), "wisdoms (chokhmot) cry aloud outside"; and as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Idra: and they are the concealed Chokhmah that is in Keter — and it is the brain of Arikh Anpin, and this is called "the concealed brain" (mocha stima'ah), which does not open even to Binah, and whose paths are not known; and this is called "the brain that rests on its dregs," which does not spread at all, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained there. However, the brain of Zeir Anpin is the emanated Chokhmah; it spreads and is revealed from the side of its paths, which spread from it to Binah; and not that it is literally revealed, but that it is not concealed like the concealment of the supernal Chokhmah that is in Keter. And we have expanded the explanation of this matter in the commentary on the Idra in the aforementioned book.

Now the emanation of the revealed Chokhmah is from the concealed Chokhmah. And now, in this, he said that the aforementioned "beginning" is Chokhmah; and because there are two Chokhmahs, as I explained, he said [it is] that revealed Chokhmah which spreads to thirty-two — unlike the concealed Chokhmah, as explained. And he said "and they came forth from that brain" — the meaning: that this Chokhmah and its thirty-two paths are emanated and found from the concealed Chokhmah that is in Keter, which is the brain of the Holy Ancient One, the brain of Arikh Anpin. And he was compelled to say so, lest we err [and] say that this Chokhmah is emanated from the essence of Keter — for if so, it would be found that the essence of Keter is revealed, and this is not so, as he expanded there [regarding] its concealment; therefore he said that its source and its emanation is from the Chokhmah that is in Keter. And some read "from that concealed [brain]" (mehahu stima'ah), the intent [being] upon the concealed Chokhmah that is in Keter; and even so, the more correct [reading is] "from that brain" (mehahu mocha), and the intent [is] the brain of Arikh Anpin. And it is possible that the true reading is "from that concealed brain" (mehahu mocha stima'ah), and it is all one matter. And the secret of "from the illumination that is in it" — the intent [is] upon the Chesed that is within the Chokhmah that is within Keter; and this matter is explained and necessitated in the Idra, as we shall explain in the book Or Yakar, in Gate 7, sign 15. "And what the Holy Ancient One illumines," etc. — two [things] were difficult for him, according to his words. One: since the emanation of Chokhmah is not from Keter, as explained, but from the aspect of the concealed Chokhmah — if so, what [does] he mean [by] "the beginning is found from the Holy Ancient One," as explained above? And to this he answered, "and what the Holy Ancient One illumines," etc., "this it is" — the meaning: that all [of] the essence of Keter [that] is revealed is only this; and since Keter has no other revelation than Chokhmah, it is fitting that we attribute its emanation to it. Again, a second [thing] was difficult for him: why did he say that Chokhmah is the "beginning," since in truth Keter and all its configurations are the beginning to all the emanated [beings]? And he answered that the intent in his saying "beginning" is not the beginning of the emanated [beings], but the beginning of the revealed [ones]; and Keter is not revealed; and this is what he said, "and the beginning was from what was revealed," the meaning [being] this Chokhmah, as explained. "And it was made into three heads" — the intent [is] upon three aspects, of which the one opposite Keter is Da'at, the second opposite Chokhmah, the third opposite Binah; and they are three brains, for the brain is always in Chokhmah, as is proved in the Zohar, and therefore the brain was made [into] three heads in three cavities, as is proved there in the Idra. "And one head includes" — the meaning: that the three of them are in Chokhmah, [corresponding] to its three aspects, included together; and it is called "the skull" (gulgalta), as explained. "And these three spread out in Zeir Anpin" — it is the totality of the Emanation down to Malkhut; and in respect of Arikh Anpin and its adornments and its configurations, the whole is called Zeir Anpin.

And the matter of its spreading in Zeir Anpin he explains further on. "And from these all is illumined" — the meaning: three lines, which are GaGaT [Gedulah-Gevurah-Tiferet], and likewise NHY [Netzach-Hod-Yesod], and they are Chesed, Din, [and] mercy, as he concludes. And the matter is that their sustenance is not literally from Keter, on account of its great concealment, except by means of this aspect, which is the brain of Zeir Anpin, as explained. And they are three roots: Chokhmah, a root to Chesed; Da'at, a root to mercy; Binah, a root to Din. "This Chokhmah was engraved," etc. — the intent [is] to explain the order of the three brains in Zeir Anpin, [namely] their being three heads that are included as one, as explained. And he said that the Chokhmah included from three heads itself was revealed and engraved and emanated Binah from within the third aspect; and therefore he said, regarding this aspect, "and it brought forth" (ve-afik), which was not said so regarding all the rest of the aspects. "And it brought forth one river" — the meaning: Binah, which is the river, and it "issues from Eden," which is Chokhmah; and the matter of "issues" is the expression "brought forth" (afik) that he stated, [in] that it is its emanation, "to water the garden," which are the seven plantings, which are the seven days of construction, as was explained. "And it entered the head of Zeir Anpin" — that is, the first brain, from below to above, in Zeir Anpin. "And there it was made into one brain; and from there it is drawn and flows into the whole body" — he means the spreading of Binah from the head of Zeir [Anpin] into the six Sefirot that are in Zeir Anpin — that is, that it is drawn from the head to water the body. And the intent is that, from the essence of Chokhmah, they are engraved in its [mode of] existence, and afterward, from its place, it is drawn to water the body — that is, into the plantings of the garden, which are the six extremities, [together] with Tiferet, called "body," in which is the vav that is in the Name; for Zeir Anpin is Tiferet, as we shall expand its explanation in the book Or Yakar. And he said that from there — from the head of Zeir Anpin that is in Tiferet, which is the totality of the three supernal [Sefirot] that are in it — Binah is drawn to water the rest of the plantings, which are the six extremities that are in it, that is, the "body," as explained. "Again, this Chokhmah was engraved," etc. — it is the aspect of Chokhmah itself; and he did not say "and it brought forth," because no new emanation [occurs], but [only] a drawing, which is the spreading of its light from the head of Zeir Anpin — that is, the aspect of the skull (gulgalta), which includes [all] three, upon Zeir Anpin — and in it a second brain was made. "That illumination which was drawn" — it is possible that it refers above and returns to Chokhmah; and the more correct [reading is] that it is drawn below, and he means: that illumination which is drawn from it [as] these two drawings — that is, Chokhmah, which includes Binah, and Chokhmah in the [mode of] existence of Chokhmah. "Were engraved" — the meaning: these two aspects were engraved into the aspect of themselves, which is Chokhmah and Binah literally; and this "engraving" is not like the engraving mentioned above, for above [it] was revealed in order to spread into Zeir Anpin, and here they were engraved into the aspect of themselves, as explained.

And the matter of this engraving and this becoming-visible is in order to unite, in order to emanate a third brain, as we shall explain, with God's help. "And they joined as one by means of one drawing," etc. — since, to explain this language, one must explain the matter of Da'at, which is a very honored and lengthy matter, and whose explanation is fine, therefore we have seen [fit] to devote to it a chapter in its own right.
In which the matter of Da'at will be explained, with the help of the One who graciously grants knowledge (chonen ha-da'at).

Da'at is what is called Tiferet, in respect of its supernal mode of existence — it is a choice and fair mode of existence. And the matter is that Keter['s] essence is the line of mercy, although it includes all three lines — the line of Chesed, the line of mercy, and the line of Din. And the examiner cannot grasp this matter until the Gate of Quiddity and Governance, in which this matter will be explained at length, with God's help.
Now, from Keter is emanated the whole line of mercy, which is Tiferet and Yesod and Malkhut, as will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with God's help.

Now Tiferet has a concealed and choice mode of existence in Keter, and that mode of existence includes the six extremities; and so it was explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (folio 220b), on the verse "all that your hand finds [to do, do with your might]," etc., "for there is no doing, nor reckoning, nor wisdom, nor knowledge [in Sheol]," etc.: and they explained, "'and knowledge' (da'at) — this is the secret of the six sides that are suspended in Thought, and they are called the world of that Thought." Thus far [their words].

The meaning: that Da'at is the secret of the concealment of the six extremities above, in Thought — the meaning: the root of the six extremities, which are six Sefirot, the six days included in the vav of the Name, whose root is concealed in the supernal source. And he said that it is called "the world of that Thought" — the meaning: "world" (olam) is the circuit (hekef), that is, the six days, which are the days of the circuit; and these, because they are the supernal circuit, are called "the world of that Thought," that is, Keter and Chokhmah — for both this and that are present in [respect of] the matter of Da'at. Further, in [Sefer] ha-Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, folio 47), these are his words: "Because the soul (neshamah) is the soul of life — Binah, which takes from Chokhmah; the vital soul (nefesh) — Malkhut, [called] Tevunah; the spirit (ruach) — Tiferet, and it is Da'at, [which] includes both; of it is said, 'and by knowledge the chambers are filled.'" Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that the soul (neshamah) is from Binah, and is called "the soul of life" because it receives from Chokhmah, which is the source of life (Ecclesiastes 7:12) — and it is written, "wisdom gives life to its possessors" — and this is what he said, "which takes from Chokhmah." "The vital soul (nefesh) — Malkhut, [called] Tevunah" — the meaning: that Malkhut, from the side of Binah, is called Tevunah; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in another place, and it will be explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions (under the entry "Tevunah"). And he intended to say this because, from the side of this aspect, it [Malkhut] is unified with Binah by means of Tiferet; and from this side it is called "nefesh," [in] that it is unified with the soul (neshamah) by means of the spirit (ruach), [namely] Tiferet, which is Da'at. And it is possible that he intended [it] because Da'at always indicates union, as will be explained; and he said that this "spirit" (ruach) is the union of Binah and Malkhut, and therefore it is called Da'at, which includes both; of it is said, "and by knowledge the chambers are filled" — and it is a great secret. And here he intended to explain to us the union of Tiferet with Binah, and he necessitated [it] from this matter: that the "chambers" are in Binah, and the chambers are the six extremities concealed in Binah, and they are a root to the six extremities, the six Sefirot of construction; and they are a house and a palace and a body to Da'at, since Da'at is a soul to them — because Da'at is the [mode of] existence of the six extremities from Chokhmah and above; and just as Chokhmah is male opposite Binah, and Binah is a palace to Chokhmah, so the six extremities — chambers ascending to a thousand thousands of thousands — are a palace to Da'at, and Da'at is a root to them, and it is a source and a root and a soul to them. And however it be, we have learned that the [mode of] existence of Tiferet is called Da'at, and it includes the six sides. Further, this matter was somewhat explained in the Ra'aya Mehemna, [where] these are his words: "And because the teru'ah is in Da'at, and it is the central pillar." Thus far. He indicated explicitly that Da'at is Tiferet — but [it must be] certainly that it is its supernal mode of existence, as we have proved from the rest of the passages. Further, in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Teitzei, folio 280b), these are his words: "'in a vision (mar'eh) I make Myself known to him' — 'in a vision': the supernal Imma makes herself known, in Da'at [which is] BeN-YaH; 'in a dream I speak with him' — the last heh." Thus far [his words].

And he said "Da'at, BeN-YaH" to indicate that it is the concealed mode of existence that lies in the bosom of father and mother, which are YaH [Yod-Heh]. And because its essence spreads within Binah, as explained — "and by knowledge the chambers are filled" — therefore the [letter-]combination of Binah is BeN-YaH. And after we have been roused to the matter of Da'at['s] being the concealed mode of existence of Tiferet, let us further preface that it is among the properties of Da'at to unite Chokhmah and Binah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 95b), [where] these are his words: "'Bereshit' — bet [means] two: Chokhmah and Binah. The third — 'the fear of YHVH [is] the beginning of knowledge (reshit da'at)'; and in this Da'at it is said, 'and the man knew (yada) Eve his wife,' for there is no coupling except through Da'at, which is the central pillar; and just as it is the central pillar — the union of Abba and Imma — so below, the Tzaddik [is] the union of the central pillar and the lower Shekhinah. And of body and covenant (guf u-vrit) it is said, 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges (de'ot),' and the two of them are testimony (edut), for there is no testimony [valid with] fewer than the two of them; and this is between (variant: and this 'son' (ben) is the union of Abba and Imma) Abba and Imma." Thus far [his words].

And this is its explanation. The intent of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in this passage is to explain that the word "Bereshit" includes three Sefirot, which are Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at. And the explanation, how: that the bet alludes to two, which are Chokhmah and Binah, which are male and female, coupling by means of Da'at, as he concludes; and this is what he said, "bet [means] two," etc. "The third — the fear of YHVH," etc. — the intent is that the letters "reshit" that remain from "Bereshit" are Da'at; and it is called "reshit" (beginning), as it is written (Proverbs 1:7), "the fear of YHVH is the beginning of knowledge (reshit da'at)"; and the intent of the verse, according to the way of the plain sense of the text, is [that] "the fear of YHVH" is a beginning to knowledge and prior to it. However, according to the interpretation of Rashbi, peace be upon him, the intent [is]: "the fear of YHVH," which is Binah, [is] "reshit," and prior to it is Da'at — for Da'at is a beginning to "the fear of YHVH," as they said, of blessed memory (Avot 2[:5]), "an empty person (bur) does not fear sin." "And in this Da'at," etc. — it was difficult for him that we should say that Da'at, which is Tiferet according to the truth, would be prior to Binah; and he brought a proof and wished to necessitate the matter, and said, "and in this Da'at," etc. It has already been explained that Adam ha-Rishon is Chokhmah, as was explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, under the entry "what is his name and what is his son's name," and Eve [is] in the place of Binah, and therefore she is called (Genesis 3:20) "the mother of all living." And he said that in this Da'at it is said (Genesis 4:1), "and the man knew (yada)," for "knew" (yada) is from the expression "Da'at" (knowledge), [in] that "there is no coupling except through Da'at." Lest we say that the meaning of "and the man knew" means the knowledge of coupling [i.e., carnal knowledge] — but [rather] this coupling was not by means of an intermediary, [therefore] to this he said "there is no coupling except through Da'at," the meaning [being]: since the expression "Da'at" is an expression of coupling, then the coupling must necessarily be by means of an intermediary, like the covenant that unites a man and his wife; and since there is no coupling except through Da'at, it is found that the coupling of Chokhmah and Binah is by means of Tiferet, called Da'at. And lest we err [and] say that, [while] it is true that the coupling and the union [are] by means of Tiferet and the secret of Da'at, even so, who compels us to say that Da'at is above Binah? — for this was the central point upon which the wheel of this whole passage turns, from its beginning to its end — to this he said, "and just as the central pillar," etc. And one must be precise: that according to the plain sense of the words it implies that his intent is to learn from Tiferet [about] Yesod, and this is the opposite of [what] reason [would expect] — for Yesod is known in the [other] Gates [as to] its action in the matter of coupling, whereas Tiferet has [only] now been newly [introduced] to us in this passage; and how can one learn the explicit from the obscure, and teach [from] that which [itself] is being taught? Rather, certainly, his intent is to necessitate that Tiferet is above Binah; and he said: just as we find union by means of Tiferet, so we find union by means of Yesod; and just as Yesod is above Malkhut, which is the female that is unified with Tiferet, the male, by its means — and it [Yesod] stands between the two of them — so, necessarily, we [must] judge regarding the matter of Tiferet, that it is certainly above Binah, [standing] between Binah and Chokhmah. And this is what he said, "just as it is the central pillar — the union of Abba and Imma," as explained, from the necessity of the verse "and the man knew"; so we find union by means of the Tzaddik, [namely] of Tiferet and Malkhut. And just as Yesod is between Tiferet and Malkhut and above Malkhut, so [there is] a necessity regarding Da'at, which is Tiferet in its concealed mode of existence, that it is above Binah, in order to unite it with its husband, who is Chokhmah. And it is found, accordingly, that Da'at is a beginning to Binah, as explained. And now, by this, the word "reshit" rightly [applies] to Tiferet, that is, in the [mode of] existence of Da'at. And he said "and the lower Shekhinah" to indicate her [mode of] existence after the accusation, [in] that she is below Yesod — [whereas] after her ascent, then she will be above Yesod; and the matter of her union then, we shall explain in the Gate of the Diminishment, with God's help. "And of body and covenant it is said, 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges'" — the meaning: he wished to necessitate the [mode of] existence of the union of Chokhmah and Binah by means of Tiferet. For [were] we to say that their union is not at all by means of it, it would be found that Tiferet is never above Binah; to this he said "body and covenant," that is, Tiferet and Yesod, and he intended to call them by the name "body and covenant" to show that, just as it [Yesod] is concealed and hidden within the body, therefore there is power in the body to unite above — as he explained in the Tikkunim, that there is no true union except by means of Yesod, and if not, it is nakedness (ervah); therefore he said "body and covenant — of them it is said, 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges (de'ot)'" — two, that is, the Da'at of Yesod and the Da'at of Tiferet. He indicated that the action of Tiferet and of Yesod is equal in [respect of] the union. And likewise, in the combination [of letters], "de'ot" (knowledges) is "edut" (testimony); and there is no testimony [valid with] fewer than two; and therefore they are necessarily two, that is, Tiferet and Yesod. And since we have necessitated that they are two witnesses [who] unite, then it is necessitated that "this is between Abba and Imma," that is, the supernal Da'at, [namely] Tiferet — for Yesod['s] union is below, [and] the reverse is not applicable; and likewise, to say that it is below the two of them is not applicable to say, as he proved; and therefore he said "and this is between Abba and Imma," literally between the two of them. Or it is possible to explain in another way [regarding] "body and covenant": that he intended to necessitate that Yesod is always above Malkhut, as he said "body and covenant," as is well known that the extension of the body is the covenant — [as] in the words of the divine [Rashbi] in many places, "body and covenant we reckon as one," etc. — to indicate that, even when the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and she [Malkhut] shall ascend to her elevated place, and Yesod shall be the tenth [below her] — even so, Yesod will, in respect of the coupling, have free passage and ascend to between the two of them, as is proved from the matter of "body and covenant," the covenant [being] between a man and his wife; and as this matter will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment, with God's help.
