"And of them it is said (1 Samuel 2:3), 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges'" — he intended to necessitate this matter from his saying "for YHVH is a God of knowledges"; and they expounded (the Sages of blessed memory, Berakhot 33b), "great is knowledge (de'ah), which was placed between two letters" — which are two Names. And if it were true that Yesod is the tenth [below Malkhut] and unites [the partners for] the coupling from the place of its dwelling [below], then there would be no "knowledge between two Names," for one of the two "knowledges" would be below, and there is no Name below it; but on the contrary, great is the Name that is between the two "knowledges" — rather, what have you to say [but] that it ascends there to the union, as explained. And he further said "and the two of them [are] testimony," etc. — the meaning: the combination [of] "de'ot" is "edut" (testimony), and there is no testimony [valid with] fewer than two — and especially in the matter of capital cases (dinei nefashot), where it is required that the two of them come and testify as one, and if not, their testimony is not combined; and this is what he said, "and there is no testimony," etc. "And this is between Abba and Imma" — the meaning: since we have necessitated that Yesod is always [present] for the union between the two unifying Sefirot, then from there we learn regarding Tiferet, that it is always [present] for the union, [as] Da'at between Abba and Imma, literally between the two of them, above Binah; and therefore it is called "reshit," [in] that it is a beginning to "the fear of YHVH," which is Binah, as explained.

And after the matter of Da'at has been explained as is fitting, and its union between Abba and Imma, let us come to explain the rest of the passage [from the Idra] that we are explaining. For Chokhmah and Binah, which are "the two drawings that were engraved," as I explained in the preceding chapter, are joined — the meaning: coupled — by means of "one drawing from the depth of the well," which is Da'at, drawn from Keter, called "the depth of the well"; and it is the supernal aspect that is in Chokhmah. And in order to draw Da'at to the third brain, they [Chokhmah and Binah] must be united by means of the drawing of the depth of the well. And the reason Keter is called "the depth of the well" is as if to say: the [mode of] existence of the well is Binah, which is called "a well," as we shall explain in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, with God's help; and from it living waters flow by means of Chokhmah, which are its walls that deepen [it]; and its depth, which is its bottom, from within which the water flows, is Keter. And by means of Da'at, which is emanated from Keter and drawn from it to between the two of them, in the essence of Chokhmah, they are united and receive one from another. And by means of Da'at, these two deeps are cleaved — this one receives and this one emanates — and there is emanated between the two of them the concealed [mode of] existence of Da'at, and it is drawn to the head of Zeir Anpin and is made into a third brain, as he explains and goes on. "And from there it is drawn and enters within the body" — this Da'at spreads within the six extremities; for Da'at is the six supernal [Sefirot], and "body" [is] the six lower [Sefirot]; and the lower [ones] are literally a body to the upper [ones], and the upper [ones] are a soul to the six lower Sefirot. And there it "fills the chambers and the halls," as explained; and the matter of "chambers and halls," this is not the place of its explanation. "And these are illumined" — the meaning: these two aspects, which are Chokhmah and Binah, are illumined by the power of the first, primordial Chokhmah, which is its aspect in Keter; and this is what he said, "from the illumination of that supernal, concealed brain," etc. — the meaning: the aspect of Chokhmah that is in Keter, which is the supernal brain and the third brain that is in Arikh Anpin. "Which is illumined by the mazal" — the meaning: that that supernal Chokhmah within Keter itself illumines, in its aspect called "mazal," which is in the Holy Ancient One, which is the concealed Chokhmah, as explained in the preceding chapter. "And all are suspended this from that," etc. — the meaning: these aspects are suspended in the secret of their aspect in Keter, Arikh Anpin; and likewise in [respect of] the matter of [drawing] sustenance, for the life of the lower [ones] is suspended in the upper [ones]. "Until it is recognized [that all is one]" — by this their unity is recognized, and they correspond [like] the loops. And although we say "Arikh Anpin" and "Zeir Anpin," even so all is one, since there is nothing above except aspects of the [mode of] existence of what is below. "And all is the Ancient One" — the meaning: these three aspects are the three supernal [Sefirot], [all] three of which are in Arikh Anpin, and from it they are drawn, and all is one, and nothing is separated from it, God forbid. "These three lights illumine three others" — the meaning: these three brains, which are three supernal aspects, emanate into GaGaT [Gedulah-Gevurah-Tiferet]; for so [is] the way of their sustenance: Gedulah from the side of Chokhmah literally, Gevurah from the side of Binah literally, Tiferet — in the secret of Da'at — from the side of the supernal aspect, [namely] Keter. And these three are called "fathers," and Netzach-Hod-Yesod are like sons in respect of them; for all that is in these is in those — except that these are "fathers" and these are "sons," these are "appointers" and these are "agents," as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places. "And all is illumined from one place" — that is, the [mode of] existence of Keter itself, in which these three aspects are concealed, in the secret of "primordial light, clear light, refined light," as will be explained in the Gate of the Refinements, with God's help. And the reason he did not mention Malkhut is because it is a female, and Zeir Anpin includes everything; and he came only to teach us the [mode of] existence of three lines drawn from three aspects — the line of Chesed from the aspect of Chokhmah, the line of Din from the aspect of Binah, the line of mercy from the aspect of Da'at and Keter, as I explained above. But Malkhut includes these three aspects, and there is nothing to say about it in respect of this inquiry. And with this, the explanation of the passage is completed. And by the way, we have learned the matter of Da'at — that its matter is not as Rabbi Shem Tov thought, who supposed [it possible] to make it a Sefirah in its own right; and the matter is not so, but [rather] it is the concealed [mode of] existence of Tiferet, as I explained at the beginning of [this] chapter. And just as it is not fitting to count [as separate Sefirot] the [other] modes of existence on their own — and the several other modes of existence that the Sefirot have, besides Tiferet, as will be explained in the Gate of Existence, with God's help — so it is not fitting to count Da'at as a Sefirah in its own right at all. And by the way, it has been explained that his saying "the place where the beginning is found" does not [mean] that there is the beginning of the Emanation and the count of the Sefirot, as he [Rabbi Shem Tov] thought, God forbid; rather, Keter is in the count of the Sefirot. However, the intent in his saying "the place where the beginning [is found]" [is]: the beginning of the revelation and the apprehension — in the manner that [the Zohar] explains it most of the time: "the beginning that stands to be questioned" [in reference] to Binah, and likewise "the beginning that stands to be questioned and to be answered" [in reference] to Chesed; and all [of this is] in [respect of] the matter of the revelation, and as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the last passage that we copied in ch.3.
And with this, this glorious Gate is concluded; and from God we ask forgiveness and pardon and atonement, for the general and for the particular. Amen.
The Fourth Gate is the Gate of Essence and Vessels.

This Gate's name attests to it: it is to explain, regarding the matter of the Sefirot, whether they are the essence of the Emanator, or [whether] they are His vessels, like vessels to the craftsman. And this is a great perplexity that fell among the later Kabbalists — that is, among the later authors, such as Rabbi Menachem Recanati and Rabbi David. And with this matter will our occupation be in this Gate, with God's help.
Chapter One.

The intent in this chapter is to copy the view of Rabbi Menachem Recanati regarding the Sefirot — whether they are essence or vessels — briefly, so far as is possible, although in the book Ta'amei ha-Mitzvot he prolonged the matter much. And we shall abridge his words and copy the essence of his proofs, and not all of them, for they are not of [what is] needed by us. And these are his words: "It is a truth in which there is no stammering [doubt], that in the Creator, blessed be He, neither multiplicity nor change can be predicated. If so, it is difficult: if the Sefirot are the essence of divinity, how can it be predicated of them that they perform judgment and mercy, the right side and the left side — for all this indicates change? Second: that in the Creator, blessed be He, limit cannot be predicated — and this is a truth in which there is no doubt; if so, how, in the Sefer Heikhalot, did they speak of limit in the Creator, blessed be He, in their saying 'from His right to His left, sixteen myriad parasangs; the measure of His stature, two hundred thirty-six thousand myriad parasangs' — all this surely indicates limit, and cannot be predicated [of Him]. And further, that in the Creator number cannot be predicated; if so, how do we say 'ten'? And further, that what is not a body is not divisible; if so, how do we say 'this is judgment and this is mercy and this mediates between them,' etc. — for all this indicates corporeality."

"Know that, in truth, the Creator, blessed be He, has no change at all, and none of the attributes of corporeality can be predicated of Him, God forbid; and all that they measured in the book of the Merkavah, they did not say of the Creator literally, but of the Sefirot. And if you say: but it is known that the power of the Emanator is in the emanated, and if so, [then] from the [same] reason for which it cannot be predicated of the Emanator, it likewise cannot be predicated of the emanated — if so, how do we say that they are in the Sefirot? — there is to say: Know that what we speak of the Sefirot, we do not say of the Creator; rather, the Sefirot are like the vessels of the craftsman, with which he performs his work — to draw a distinction many times over. And the Sefirot are equal to a thing and its opposite. And to bring the matter near to the intellect, the sages compared it to the will of the soul, which is equal to all the desires and to all the thoughts that spread from it; and although they are many, their root is only one, and the soul does not change — rather, the change is in the body, which brings the thought of the soul into actuality. And therefore there is to say that they are things equal to a thing and its opposite, for if we did not say so, there would not be in them the power for every thing. And therefore they compared them to the will of the soul; and just as the soul is clothed by the body, so the Creator, blessed be He — from His great light these vessels sparkled, and the sages called them 'Sefirot'; and the spreading of the First Cause into these vessels is called Emanation." Thus far [his words].

And he brought a passage [as] a proof for his words; and since it is not of the matter, we have not copied it. And let us return to his words: "And the Sefirot do not delimit Him; rather, they receive the effluence from Him first, more than all the rest of the created [beings]; and God forbid that there be in them body or corporeality — rather, they are kinds of light, like the light that issues from the eye, which is not apprehended or grasped, for it is nothing; but [only] the thing apprehended, after the light, is grasped in the depiction of the heart's thoughts, and that form is depicted by the power of the attribute. And behold, I add for you, with many proofs from the words of our Sages of blessed memory, that all that they spoke of the Sefirot is not fitting to say of Him, blessed be He. And I found in the wondrous Zohar (Naso, folio 137b), these are its words: 'Thus it is taught: it is not enough for the wicked that they do not turn the attribute of judgment into the attribute of mercy, but that they [even] turn the attribute of mercy into the attribute of judgment? And how do they turn [it]? — but is it not written, "I, YHVH, have not changed"? Rather: at every time that the Ancient of Ancients, the white head, is revealed, the delight-in-delightings is revealed, [and] great mercies are found in all. And at the time it is not revealed, all the judgments of Zeir Anpin are ready; and, as it were, mercy performs judgment — that Ancient One of all. For it is taught: when the Ancient of Ancients, the delight-in-delightings, is revealed, all the lamps that are called by this name are illumined, and mercy is found in all. And at the time the concealed of the concealed is not revealed, and these lamps are not illumined, judgments are roused and judgment is performed. Who caused this judgment? — the delight-in-delightings that is not revealed. And therefore the wicked turn mercy into judgment.' Thus far the Zohar. And 'do not make yourself as one dozing' in your reading of this — for if you are precise in the passage, you will find that it proves that the Sefirot are not literally the essence of the Creator; for if not so, what did it answer, 'Rather, at every time that the Ancient of Ancients,' etc.? — since, in the end, it said, 'and at the time it is not revealed.' Rather, it appears that the judgment is [present] in the concealment of His face, blessed be He, from a Sefirah, and then it would be consumed of itself. A parable [of] a king who commanded one of his servants, 'When you see a man swift in his work, you shall surely endow him from your threshing-floor and your winepress,' and commanded another, 'When you see a lazy man, strike him' — and behold, the king neither does evil nor does good to either of them; rather, all is by his command. So He, blessed be He, emanates into the attributes to perform actions, and He does not change His actions. Further, in the Zohar (there, folio 136), these are his words: 'In the cavities of the skull, three cavities are found, in which a brain dwells, and a thin membrane that covers them — but not a hard, concealed membrane like the Ancient of Days; and therefore this brain spreads and issues to thirty-two paths; this is what is written, "and a river issues from Eden." And it is taught: in the three cavities of the skull a brain dwells; from one cavity there bursts and spreads one wellspring to four directions, and there issues from that brain that dwells in this cavity thirty-two paths, spirits of wisdom. From the second cavity there bursts and spreads another wellspring, and fifty gates are opened; from these fifty gates are bound the fifty days of the Torah, and the fifty years of the Jubilee, [and] the fifty thousand generations that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to return the spirit to him and to make it dwell in him. From the third cavity there issue a thousand thousands [of] chambers and halls, upon which Da'at dwells, and dwells in them; and this cavity sets its dwelling between this cavity and that cavity, and all those chambers are filled from two sides; this is what is written, "and by knowledge the chambers are filled." And these three cavities spread out in the whole body, to this side and to that side; and in them the whole body is bound, and the body is bound in them on all its sides; and in the whole body they spread and are found,' etc., until: 'and in this are suspended the right and the left, light and darkness, mercy and judgment; and all the right and the left are suspended in this and not in the Ancient One.' Thus far [his words]."

And we have seen [fit] to abridge it, and not to copy the interpretation of Rabbi Menachem, of blessed memory, upon it — for he did not delve into it at all, but [gave only] the surface of the passage, and the rest of the passage neither raises nor lowers [anything]. And let us return to his words: "Contemplate this matter greatly, and turn it over in your thought, and you will see that he removed the attributes [predicates] from Him, blessed be He, in that he said 'in this they are suspended, and not in the Ancient One'; for of the Creator, blessed be He, one cannot say 'light' or 'darkness' or any of the opposites, which are attributed only to the attributes [Sefirot]; and if we say that the attributes are the essence of divinity, how did he say 'and not in the Ancient One'? — Behold, we have in this matter two proofs. Further, a third proof, in the Zohar (Bamidbar, folio 120), in this language: 'Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Shimon his father; he said to him: a sign for the coupling of union — whence [is it]? He said to him: My son, although we have established matters for each and every side, and they were scattered — here a matter and there a matter — take this sign in your hand, and so it is: like the circuit of the altar, as we have learned, "he comes to the southeast corner, [then] the northeast, [then] the northwest, [then] the southwest," etc.' And we must explain the question and the answer; and with this our intent will be explained, with God's help. 'A sign for the coupling' — the meaning: how shall a person emanate to the head of the Tzaddik, and which attribute receives before its fellow, [and] how is the order of the union. And Rabbi Shimon answered that a person must first unite the east, which is Tiferet, with the south, which is Chesed — for it is the attribute of mercy; but not so much as the Chesed, because the attribute of judgment is emanated there, which is north, as it is said (Jeremiah 1:14), 'from the north the evil shall break forth'; and afterward one needs also the east with the north, for it receives from both of them; afterward one must join the wife to her husband by way of the attribute of judgment, which receives first, from the north by way of the east; and afterward one must unite her with the south, by way of the attribute of mercy, so that she shall not separate from the supernal waters and become the harsh attribute of judgment. And because the Shekhinah receives last, therefore they said that the Shekhinah is in the west — that is, for there the effluence and the blessing, the attribute of judgment and [the attribute] of mercy, are mingled; and then the blessings are found above and below. And I found a support for this order in the matter of the union [in] what is written (Song of Songs 4:16), 'awake, O north, and come, O south,' etc.; and see how it explained here that the garden, which is likened to the Shekhinah, receives first from the north and afterward from the south, as it is said, 'awake, O north, and come, O south, [that] my garden [may breathe out]' — the meaning: to draw the blessing to the dry garden and to water it from the waters of repentance and mercy. And all this effluence and this drawing comes entirely from the Creator, blessed be He, by the spreading of the Cause of Causes into the attributes, which is called 'the union,' and it is the Emanation, as I explained above. And so that you may be expert in the corners [directions], he said, 'take a sign,' etc. And it appears to me that from here we may say that the extremities are not joined to Him, blessed be He — for if so, they would not need the effluence and the blessing, if He, blessed be He, and the Sefirot were one essence, as we explained above. And since the emanated is not separated from the Emanator, we have to say that it was not of the Creator that they said that there is in Him neither joining nor separation, but [only] of the attributes." Further, Rabbi Menachem brought proofs from the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya; and since they are not such [strong] proofs, I have not written them; and likewise from the Sefer ha-Bahir.

Now we have completed what was in our mind to copy from the words of Rabbi Menachem; and likewise Rabbi Yehudah Chayyat copied his words at length in his book Minchat Yehudah, and added to him a little — small, not great — and said that, although the law is according to the words of Rabbi Menachem, even so, that which he necessitated from the matter of the parasangs stated in the book of the Merkavah — the intent is not literal parasangs, in a quantitative sense, God forbid, but [rather] the expression is derived from the expression (Daniel 5:28) "your kingdom is divided (peres)," and the intent [is] sparks spreading from Him to every side. And Rabbi Yehudah took issue with Rabbi Menachem regarding the interpretation of the passage of the union as well, [and] likewise regarding what he wrote in the likeness of "the light that issues," etc.; and Rabbi Yehudah set forth another parable, and said: like the likeness of the spark of the sun's light and its light, which is not the essence of the sun but a property in it — so the Emanation is a property in the Emanator, and is not the essence of the Emanator. Thus far have the words of the one who says that the Sefirot are vessels reached, in brief.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, written the view of the one who says that the Sefirot are vessels — namely Rabbi Menachem, and Rabbi Yehudah followed after him — our intent in this chapter is to copy the view of Rabbi David, in the book Magen David, who held that they are the essence of divinity. And because the objections that we brought from Rabbi Menachem in the preceding chapter were difficult for him, he resolved [them] and said: "Know that the variation of the names, or the number of the Sefirot, does not necessitate multiplicity in the Creator, blessed be He, God forbid. For the one who said, by the Name Ehyeh, that it indicates perfect mercy, and by the Name Elohim, that it indicates justice and judgment, and likewise in the significations of the rest of the Sefirot and their allusions — this is nothing but the variation of the aspects, in [their] being joined to differing actions. That is, when you examine the essence of divinity from the side that it indicates perfect mercy — that is, that it performs the action of mercy — you call it by the Name Ehyeh; and when you examine it from the side that it indicates judgment and justice — that is, that it performs the [acts of] justice — you call it by the Name Elohim. And likewise in the Sefirot and in the rest of the names: that there is here nothing but one essence, in the utmost of unity and simplicity, which, according to the variation of the aspects in it, in [their] being joined to its differing actions, is called by many names, and it is said of it that it is ten Sefirot. And let it not carry you away [to think] that this necessitates multiplicity in the Creator, blessed be He — for these are said by way of the analogy of His essence, blessed be He, to His created [beings]." Thus far [his words].

And afterward he aimed to necessitate this with philosophical proofs, and we have not copied them, on account of the smallness of their usefulness. And he brought a proof that the Sefirot are the essence of divinity from the Zohar (Ha'azinu, folio 297), [where] these are its words: "'For I call upon the name of YHVH' — what is 'for I call upon the name of YHVH'? Rabbi Shimon said: behold it is written, 'ascribe greatness to our God,' etc. 'Ascribe greatness' — this is Gedulah. 'The Rock, His work is perfect' — this is Gevurah. 'For all His ways are judgment' — this is Tiferet. 'A God of faithfulness' — this is Netzach. 'And without iniquity' — this is Hod. 'Righteous' — this is Yesod. 'And upright' — this is Malkhut. He is all the holy Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. And therefore 'for I call upon the name of YHVH,' etc. Rabbi Chiya said: from this verse I have learned supernal wisdom, and so it is; but the end of the verse binds the bond of faith, in what is written, 'He' (Hu), as it is said, 'righteous and upright is He' — that is to say, He is all, He is one without separation. For lest you say [that] all these are many, it returned and said 'He' — they all ascend and are bound and unified in one. And all is 'He': He was, and He is, and He will be; and He is one — blessed be His name forever and unto the ages of ages." Thus far [its words].

Here you have a clear proof for what we have said. For he said that the end of the verse, in the word "He" (Hu), binds all the Sefirot together in a firm bond — to show that, although the Sefirot are many in number, ten, from the side of the aspect toward His actions, even so we may say that they are "He," that is, [that] they are the essence of the Name, blessed be He, who is unique in the utmost of unity, to the point that it is said of Him "He." And therefore he said, "lest you say [that] they are many" — that is, lest you say that all these Sefirot are many, and if so, how is it possible that they be one thing — therefore he answered him, [in] that the verse said "He" after it mentioned the ten Sefirot, to indicate that they are unified in His essence, blessed be He, and the multiplicity is in [their] being joined to the recipients, in differing aspects. And this is a great proof. And it is impossible to make it known to you without my explaining to you the intent of the Zohar: for at first it mentioned the attributes in particular, and afterward included them under one name.

Now, "for the name of YHVH" alludes to the first three. "Ascribe greatness to our God" — Chesed is called Gedulah. "The Rock, His work is perfect" — this alludes to the Fear of Isaac, which is mighty and strong. "For all His ways are judgment" — alludes to Tiferet, etc. And after the allusion [to] the whole spreading, he returned and included it in complete union in the word "He" — that is to say, these Sefirot, which are ten in respect of the recipients, are thus literally "He," that is, the essence of divinity, simple in the utmost. Further, he brought a proof from a mishnah in Sefer Yetzirah, from the matter of the depths, which we explained above in the Gate of [the question] whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. And he said that, after it mentioned all the Sefirot, it said that the Name is unique in them; and if so, they are the essence of divinity literally. Further, he brought a proof from another mishnah, "ten Sefirot of belimah: their end is fixed in their beginning and their beginning in their end," etc., "that a unique Lord, and He has no second. And before one, what do you count?" — that is to say, [although] the Sefirot are ten in respect of differing aspects, even so the end is fixed in the beginning, for the head is the end and the end is the head, from the side of the abundance of their unity in the essence of the Creator; and YHVH, blessed be He, is unique in them, and there is no duality there, God forbid, to the point that no number or multiplicity may be attributed to Him, God forbid — and this is their saying, "before one, what do you count?" — for one cannot say [anything] except that He is one, one in the utmost of unity. Further, a proof (from Midrash Rabbah, Shemot, ch.3) on the verse "and they say to me, what is His name?" Rabbi Abba bar Memel said: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "My name you wish to know? — according to My deeds I am called. Sometimes I am called by El Shaddai, by Tzeva'ot, by Elohim, by Adonai," etc. "When I judge the creatures, I am called Elohim," etc.

Behold, this Midrash is literally a necessitation for what we have said: that YHVH, blessed be He, is one, and if we take Him in respect of His actions in the created [beings], thus is He called by His differing names. Further, he brought a proof from the Zohar (Bereshit, folio 19b), on the verse "I went down into the garden of nuts": "And the whole world is like this kind [of thing], above and below — from the head of the secret of the supernal point to the end of all the grades, all of it is [one], this within that and that within that, until it is found that this is a husk to that and that to that. The primordial point is an inner illumination that has no measure [by which] to know its purity and fineness and clarity, until it spread a spreading; and that spreading of that point became one palace, for that point to be clothed [in it] — an illumination that is not known, for the abundance of its purity. The palace, which is a garment to that concealed point, is an illumination that has no measure; and even so, it is not [so] fine and pure as that primordial point, hidden and concealed. That palace spread a spreading [of] primordial light; and that spreading is a garment to that palace, [which is itself] fine and pure, more inward. From here onward, this spreads in that and is clothed in that, until it is found that this is a garment to that and that to that — this [is] brain and that [is] husk. And although this is a garment, it becomes brain to another grade. And all is made in this manner below, until [it is found] that a human being in this world is brain and husk, body and spirit; and all is the rectification of the world." Thus far [its words].

Now, when you contemplate this passage well, you will understand the saying of the masters of Kabbalah, who called YHVH, blessed be He, "a soul to souls" — for He, blessed be He, is a soul to His attributes, which are called "souls"; for the upper [one] is a soul to that [one] below, and each [is a soul] to its fellow; and they are unified in a complete, true union.

And the matter of the parable of the soul is this: that, just as the soul of a person is one, and we cannot apprehend its truth except by its actions that appear in the limbs of the body, so — to draw a distinction [of] a thousand thousands of thousands, without end — we cannot apprehend Him, blessed be He, except from the side of His actions performed by means of His attributes. And just as there is no action for the limbs of the body without the soul, for it is their life and their cause, so there is no action for the attributes without the will of their Possessor, blessed be He, for He is the cause of their endurance. And just as the soul is one, and its powers are bound up in it and are the essence of the soul — except that it has differing names according to the origins of its actions, and therefore it is sometimes called "vital" (chiyyunit) and sometimes "natural" (tiv'it) and sometimes "psychic" (nafshit), [these] being powers chained-down from the essence of the simple soul — so the Sefirot are unified in the essence of the Creator, blessed be He, and the multiplicity and the variation is in respect of the actions chained-down from the unity of the Creator; not that there is any variation in Him, but [only] in respect of the recipients. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory (Berakhot 10[a]) likened the soul to the Holy One, blessed be He, in five things." Thus far [his words].

And he further prolonged with proofs from Rav Chamai and Rabbeinu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, and Rabbeinu Bachya, of blessed memory — that is to say, that they all agree with his view. And in truth, neither the words of the Zohar nor the words of the commentators agree with his view, [and] all the more [is there no] necessity for that view; for with a little examination a person can contemplate that all his proofs — the wind will carry them all away, and there is no substance in them. And in truth, we have copied [only] the most nearly-approaching of his proofs to his view. And not enough [is] this, but that he prolonged against Rabbi Menachem and nullified some of his proofs in a tongue not soft but [in] bone-breaking [fashion]; and even so, let us copy here some of his answers to the difficulties of Rabbi Menachem. He resolved that number does not befall Him, blessed be He, from the side of His essence, but [only] from the side of the division of the aspects; and likewise the division of the attributes, and branch and root, and judgment and mercy, and right and left — all these things are said of Him, blessed be He, and of His essence, and there is no deficiency in His essence, for they are not said of Him, blessed be He, from the side of His absolute essence, but [only] from the side of what is examined in differing aspects. And understand this. And we have no need of his view; for how could we say it [otherwise]? — since it is well known in all the books of Kabbalah, and he too will admit this, that the Sefirot are emanated and not created; and it is known that everything of which "emanation" is said is the power of the Emanator in the emanated, and the emanated is not separated from the Emanator; and if so, all that is said of the Sefirot is literally said of the Creator, blessed be He. And how can he divide [and say] that they said [it] of the Sefirot and not of the Creator — since it is His essence, blessed be He? And he already touched upon this and magnified the difficulty, and answered in the aforementioned way; and what he answered is no answer to this difficulty. And how shall that which he said in Sefer Yetzirah be settled — that they are in a wondrous unity, "like a flame bound to a coal"? And how shall we also resolve the rest of the passages that he stated above?

And further, [in] that, in what he resolved, he returned to the perplexity: for if we say [there is] division in His attributes and multiplicity, then they would necessitate multiplicity in Him, blessed be He, when He is described by them, since they are distinct from Him.

And further, [in] that the parable of the soul that he brought above — which is "equal to all the desires," etc. — is the opposite of his intent: for since the Sefirot are not the essence of divinity, how do they spread from Him, their root being one? — for, according to his view, they are separate from Him. And the passages that he brought are the opposite of his intent, and a proof for our words. The first passage: "but is it not written, 'I, YHVH, have not changed'; if so, how do they turn His attributes?" — since His attributes and He, blessed be He, are all one thing, [then] how do you say that they turn [them]? Know that the Tanna said only "mercy into judgment," for if not so, what was difficult for him? Rather, certainly, since the attributes are His essence, therefore he found it difficult, [in] that even [of] the attributes it is not fitting to say they "turn" [them]. And as for the matter of all the passages, the resolution [is] that all the things he said — judgment and mercy, right and left, north and south — all these things are from the side of His aspect, not from the side of His essence; rather, from the side of the concealment of His face He performs judgment from His essence, and then we say that He is "judgment"; and when He emanates, the intent is whitened toward mercy, and then we say that He is "mercy." Thus far the words of Rabbi David. And even so, he wished to overturn the proofs and the passages; and since this matter neither raises nor lowers [anything] for our view, we have seen [fit] to abridge. And in truth, most of his objections against Rabbi Menachem have no place. For Rabbi Menachem said that what they said — that they are the Emanation and the power of the Emanator, etc. — is specifically [in reference] to His providence that spreads within His Sefirot, but not [to] the Sefirot [themselves]. And likewise, that which he objected from the matter of the parable of the soul that Rabbi Menachem set forth, etc. — his intent is not as he explained in the words of Rabbi Menachem; rather, the intent of Rabbi Menachem was to resolve, regarding the matter [that] the attributes are ten and the actions are without end — and to this his intent was to say that each and every attribute performs a thing and its opposite, like the soul, for if not so, it would be fitting that the Sefirot be without end, like the actions, which have no end; and this is certainly a mighty difficulty for Rabbi David. And when we are precise in the words of Rabbi Menachem, we find this matter explained, and these are his words: "and the Sefirot are things equal to a thing and its opposite." And the intent is that the Sefirot themselves sometimes punish [and] sometimes reward; and the reason is that the one who fulfills the commandment of the covenant, which is dependent on Yesod — that attribute will surely give him good reward for his labor, and his reward will be by its means, as we find (in the Zohar, Miketz, 197) regarding Joseph the Righteous — because he fulfilled the commandment of guarding the covenant, he ate the fruit of his deeds in this world, and merited kingship, and to sustain the whole world, in the manner of Yesod, which nourishes and sustains the world. And likewise, if a man sins in this commandment and profanes his covenant, behold, by means of Yesod will his punishment surely be. And regarding this matter our Sages of blessed memory said (Sotah 8b), "with the measure that a person measures, it is measured out to him" — the intent [being] that, according to the blemish blemished by his hand, so will his punishment be, by means of that attribute. And we shall not trouble ourselves with the explanation of this matter here, because it is appointed for the Gate of Quiddity and Governance, with God's help. And likewise, that which he objected against Rabbi Menachem — that if they are vessels, how is He, blessed be He, described by them? — this too is no difficulty; for according to him, is it well [resolved]? — if they are aspects, how is He described, etc.? Rather, what is there to say [but] that they are in respect of the recipients, in the manner of the sun that melts and dries, etc., and it is in respect of the recipients; and also, according to this [view], in divinity, etc., as is explained from within his words — likewise, according to the words of Rabbi Menachem, we shall resolve that they are in respect of the aspects of the Sefirot, not in respect of Him, blessed be He; and although He is described by them, the intent is [His] being [the one who] acts by means of them. Thus far what we have seen [fit] to explain in the words of Rabbi Menachem and Rabbi David, without the pursuit of length, but [in] utmost brevity. And we shall not trouble ourselves with the settling of the passages from within which they necessitated their proof, because neither side of this inquiry disputes with our intent.

And further, [in] that all those passages incline to this side and to that side, and there is from them no necessity, neither for this [view] nor for that, as will be seen from them by light examination.

After we have, in the preceding chapters, set forth these two arrays — namely the view of Rabbi Menachem, that they are vessels, and the view of Rabbi David, that they are essence — let us now rouse, in this chapter, our short and weak opinion upon them. The first array, which was arrayed in chapter 1 — the view of Rabbi Menachem, and the view of Rabbi Yehudah Chayyat following after him — and it is this: that the Sefirot are the vessels of the craftsman, [for him] to perform by means of them, as he wills, a thing and its opposite; and the good actions and their opposites are all chained-down from the attributes, which are His vessels, and not from His essence, God forbid. And there is [reason] to rouse [an objection] against this view. Behold, it is known that the knowledge of the Name, blessed be He, is not like the knowledge of the rest of the created [beings]; for they know with a knowledge outside themselves. The example of this [is] a person who knows a form among the forms, or some thing that is depicted in his mind: behold, in any case there will be three things. One: the knowledge [faculty] that was devoid of that form before his knowing it — that is one; and the knowledge by which he knew and recognized that form — that is two; and the known form — that is three; and they are called the knowledge, the knower, [and] the known. And the knowledge of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so, God forbid; rather, He is the knowledge, and He is the knower, and He is the known, as will be explained at length in the Gate of Quiddity and Governance, in ch.13, with God's help. And if so, since this premise is true and fitting to be fixed in the heart of the believers, how can our saying be valid that the Sefirot are not His essence? — for behold, God forbid, He would be knowing by a wisdom outside Himself, God forbid, God forbid; and likewise, how would He be understanding by a Binah outside Himself, God forbid? And in this manner we infer regarding the rest of the Sefirot attributed to the rest of the actions. Further, according to his view, that the reward and the punishment are chained-down from the attributes — for of divinity it cannot be predicated, neither light nor darkness, neither judgment nor mercy, etc. — if so, it is found, accordingly, that the attributes are the rewarders and the punishers by their nature, which their Emanator implanted in them, as he said, "a parable [of] a king who commanded one of his servants," etc. — if so, according to this view, God forbid, there is in divinity no capacity of the rewarder and the overseer, but [rather] YHVH has abandoned the earth into the hand of the attributes; and if a man sins, his prayer before the Emanator will not avail to emanate good to him and to forgive his offense, since his reward and his punishment do not depend on Him, but [rather] let him pray to that servant whom the king appointed over the reward and the punishment. For if we should wish to say, according to his view, that when a person prays to the Cause of Causes, He receives his prayer and commands the servant to do good to him and to remove his evil from before his face — if so, it would be found that by His command and His will are the life and the good and the death and the evil, the reward and the punishment, and He changes from will to will: before his prayer He desired his destruction and to punish him, and now He desires his endurance and his life and his good. Rather, what have you to say, according to his view? — [that] the life and the good and the opposite are all handed over into the hand of the attributes, which is the faithful servant likened [to] above; and with this, God forbid, His providence, blessed be He, is removed from the world, and likewise our worship before Him is removed — for before Him all are equal in [respect of] good, the righteous like the wicked, since there is in His will no examination [distinction] between good and evil, God forbid. And these things, and the like of them, are the demolition of faith, God forbid, and not its establishment. And it is clear to us that Rabbi Menachem, of blessed memory, was of those steeped in perfect faith. Further, there is [reason] to be precise [in objecting] to this view: that since the essence of divinity is not the rewarder and the punisher — for the reason that no change of will is found in Him — if so, accordingly, He is devoid of the capacity to do good and to do evil, for He removed His capacity and handed it to that servant. For if you do not say so, according to his view, but [say] rather that it is within His capacity to reward and to punish, it is found, accordingly, that there is in Him a change of will, for from the change of will follow the reward and the punishment and the judgment and the mercy. And since He has no change of will, it is found that it is not within His capacity to judge for liability or for merit; for the liability follows from the will of judgment to do evil to that liable man, to destruction, and the merit and the reward follow by reason of the change of His will toward the doing-of-good and the success of that upright man; and as a person changes from the good way to the evil way, so the judgment changes upon him, and as he changes from the evil [way] to the good [way], so the judgment changes toward him, whether for good or for evil. It is found, accordingly, that this matter does not depend on His knowledge and His will — but rather, the one whom He [finds] good from his beginning, He does good to him, even if he changes to evil; and the one who [is] evil at his beginning, He does evil to him, even if he changes to good — and all these things are against uprightness and righteousness. And now it would be found, accordingly, God forbid, that the whole Torah was not given by God, but by His servants — for in it is written reward and punishment, and in particular in the verse (Deuteronomy 28:63), "and it shall be, just as YHVH rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so YHVH will [cause others to] rejoice over you to destroy you and to annihilate you" — for these are nothing but the words of a servant among His servants, since there is in God no change of will, neither to do good nor to do evil; and likewise the majority of the essentials of the Torah. And may the Merciful One save us from this view! For this is nothing but the view of the philosophers, who speak of God [in] error, fabricating from their heart deception and falsehood; and of them it is said (Psalms 139:20), "who speak of You with wicked intent (li-mzimah)," etc. — for they exchange their glory for shame. And surely we have to believe that this is not the intent of the pious Rabbi Menachem, of blessed memory; rather, surely another spirit was with him, and the hand of his tongue fell short in his transferring [it] from the intellect to the mouth and from the mouth to the pen — for it is known to all who see his books, his piety and his uprightness; and "if the animal of the righteous — the Holy One, blessed be He, does not bring a mishap by means of [it], the righteous themselves all the more so." Rather, surely the correct [thing] is to believe that this was not his intent, according to the plain sense understood from his words, God forbid.

And further, there is [reason] to object against the masters of this view, the like of these and these; but it is not fitting to prolong [discussion] in these matters, for the honor of our Fashioner. And even this it would not have been fitting to raise in writing, except in order to remove the weak of understanding from error, God forbid; and may God atone. And [now] to the second array, which Rabbi David, of blessed memory, arrayed, and [in which] he wished to rely on the view of Rav Hai and Rav Chamai and the author of the Ma'arekhet — and it is that the Sefirot are the essence of divinity; however, the multiplicity is not from His side, blessed be He, but [only] from the side of the aspect of His actions toward us, in the likeness of the sun — for so he explained at the end of his words, when one examines [them] in his book. And regarding this matter we say: "how this man neither ails nor feels, and as though sleeping and lying down he said it!" For since the existence of the Sefirot is [merely] the aspect of the actions, in the likeness of the sun, as explained — if so, why should it be necessary that Malkhut receive from Tiferet, and any [other] attribute from another besides it, since they are [merely] from the side of the aspect of His actions, blessed be He, and they are all grasped in His essence, in the likeness of the light of the sun, as explained? If so, it cannot be validly said of Him that the attribute of His being a dryer needs the attribute of His being a melter — for this would not be necessary in order that its fellow be emanated from it and this one draw sustenance from that, since they are all equal in [respect of] good: Keter equal to Malkhut, and Malkhut to Keter, and likewise all of them. It is found, accordingly, that the matter of the channels, and the grades of the worlds, and their binding and their union one with another, and likewise the order of their emanation, is nullified — for they have no order, since they are all bound in Him like one man, in the likeness of the sun, whose attributes are bound up in itself, not an attribute in [another] attribute, as explained.

Now Rabbi David wished to support himself from what is said in the Zohar, "this is brain to that and that is husk to that" — and it is opposed to his words in every [respect], as explained; for according to his view there is no attribute that needs another besides it, or [else] they would all be brains or all husks. And likewise he wished to support himself from the words of the Geonim and the commentators; and his view does not agree with any one of them, as is explained to the examiner in their books, of blessed memory. Further, it is difficult: for according to this view, the whole intent of prayer and the commandments and the unification of the worlds, one with another, is nullified.

Now he aimed to establish the corner[stone] of unity — and the like, [which] he [had] demolished; for the intent of the verse "Hear, O Israel," etc., is to unite the Sefirot together, and in the word "one" (echad) to unite Malkhut with all of them, and all of them with Malkhut, and to raise her by way of the rungs by which she descended. And according to his view, neither "the diminishment of the moon" nor "and the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun" is applicable there.

And further, if so — since the Sefirot are [there only] when you examine [them] in respect of their actions — then the Sefirot are not found except at the time the actions are performed. The example: you find the existence of the Sefirah of Chesed [in] its performing the action of Chesed; and when its action is removed, that attribute is removed; it is found that sometimes they are ten, when He performs all His actions, and sometimes they are five or two, all according to the measure of His actions; and sometimes, too, they ascend above ten, when His actions are multiplied in this world. And even if it is possible to settle, with some strain, a few of these our questions, even so the words of truth are recognizable.

And further, there is [reason] to be precise: that, according to his view, [in] that the Sefirot are only from the side of the examination of His actions toward the recipients — if so, it is found that the Sefirot are not found in the true [mode of] existence; and if so, what is expounded in the Zohar regarding the matter of the Sefirot and the fineness of those worlds, and in particular in the Idra of Naso and in the Idra of Ha'azinu — toward which, surely, the longing of the soul is directed [and] nothing [else] — [would be void].

And further, [in] that it is explained in several places in the Zohar regarding the matter of the soul and its emanating, by means of its deeds, from the Sefirot to the worlds, and its ascent to cleave, by way of its deeds, to its honored roots, which are the Sefirot. And according to his view, that the Sefirot are only as [stated] above, behold, it will not cleave to anything at all — for they are not Sefirot except in respect of the actions, in the likeness of the sun, of which we cannot say that there is in it the existence of attributes; and likewise in divinity there are no Sefirot, God forbid; and by what would the souls be unified? Can we say that they would be unified in the divine essence [itself]? — this, surely, [is] not [so]. And these things, and the like of them, are the demolition of the wisdom and its cessation. And now, where is the one who counts, and where is the one who weighs? — [every] concealed inquiry among the inquiries of the wisdom is rejected, [and] the majority of its corners[tones].

And behold, Rabbi David demolished a wall in order to bring in a mat — for, on account of one perplexity in which he was perplexed in the wisdom, he demolished the majority of its corners[tones]. Thus far has reached what we have seen [fit] to rouse against the view of Rabbi Menachem and Rabbi David; and with this, this chapter is concluded.
